Health benefits

About IcePanel

WestartedIcePanelbecauseexistingtoolsforsoftwarearchitecturesuck.

They’re slow, overcomplicated, and built for managers to enforce process, not for engineers to actually enjoy using.

At our previous jobs, we spent too much time in meetings talking about architecture and not enough time actually building. Diagrams got stale, decisions got lost, and nothing felt connected to reality.

So we started building something better. It began as a side project, let us snowboard most days in Whistler for a season, and people kept using it…We got to nearly $1M USD with just the founders before we hired.

Today we’re a small, profitable team ($4.5M+ CAD ARR) building a collaborative modelling tool for software architecture. We care about staying lean, shipping fast, having fun, and building something peopleactuallylove.

How we work

  • - We keep meetings to a minimum
  • - We ship weekly
  • - We work in small teams (usually 2 people) with clear ownership
  • - We avoid over-engineering, but we care deeply about polish
  • - We release early, get feedback, and refine

This is not a place to hide. You’ll own what you build.

The role

You’ll build across the entire product:

  • - Frontend UI/UX (working closely with design)
  • - Backend APIs and data models
  • - Real-time systems (WebSockets)
  • - Infrastructure and migrations
  • - Fixing, refining, and improving what already exists

Our stack: TypeScript, Node.js, Vue, Pixi.js, Tailwind, Cloud Run, Firestore, WebSockets

What “great” looks like

A great hire doesn’t wait to be told what to do.

In your first couple of weeks, you’ll use the product, find something that feels off, and fix it.

Not because it was assigned. Because it bothered you.

You’ll own meaningful features end-to-end. Examples:

  • - Git-like workflows for diagramming
  • - Import and data ingestion pipelines
  • - Access controls for complex organizations
  • - Data visualization across large architectures

You’ll make things feel better, not just work.

30 / 60 / 90 days

First 30 days

  • - Get familiar with the product and codebase
  • - Ship improvements to areas that feel “off”
  • - Start contributing to real features

60 days

  • - Take ownership of a meaningful area of the product
  • - Improve performance or usability in a noticeable way
  • - Work across frontend + backend without hand-holding

90 days

  • - Own and ship a complex feature end-to-end
  • - Contribute to solving harder problems like:
  • - Access control for large organizationsManaging deeply nested architecture models
  • - Performance issues with highly connected systems

Current challenges

  • - Changing model hierarchies (parents/levels) is complex and fragile
  • - Large, highly connected models can impact real-time performance
  • - Access permissions don’t scale well for large companies
  • - LLM assisted architecture documentation and ideation

If those sound interesting, you’ll probably enjoy this.

About you

You:

  • - Have 6+ years of experience across both large companies and startups
  • - Are strong in both frontend and backend
  • - Have built things you’re genuinely proud of
  • - Care deeply about how things look and feel, not just that they work
  • - Take ownership and don’t wait for permission
  • - Are comfortable working across a large, evolving codebase
  • - Can take feedback without ego and adjust quickly

You’ve likely:

  • - Built side projects just because something annoyed you
  • - Worked across product, UX, and engineering boundaries
  • - Shipped real features that people use

Proof of craft (required)

You must show us something you’ve built.

  • - Portfolio, live apps, screenshots - anything that shows off your skills
  • - We care about how it feels to use, not just what it does

If you can’t point to something you’ve built that feels great, this role isn’t for you.

You’ll struggle here if

  • - You rely heavily on AI without understanding fundamentals
  • - You wait for direction instead of taking initiative
  • - You blame others instead of owning problems
  • - You lead with ego instead of curiosity
  • - You need constant permission to move forward

Also, if you don’t actually care about what you’re building, don’t apply.

Bonus points

  • - You’ve been a founder (even if it failed)
  • - You come from a non-traditional background
  • - You understand the limits of LLMs beyond surface-level use
  • - You’ve spent time in a major tech hub and chose (or want) to work in Canada

Location

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
ROLE OVERVIEW

As a Senior Product Manager at HealthVerity, you’ll play a key role in shaping and delivering Data Products that make a difference. You’ll work closely with cross-functional teams—including Sales, Marketing, Data Product Design, Engineering, Data Partnerships, Pricing, Delivery, and Commercial Operations—to bring innovative and impactful Data Products to market, inspiring growth for the business.

You’ll connect directly with our core customers and their unique personas across the pharmaceutical, government, pharma services, and data partner sectors, ensuring that their voices and needs are integrated into our product development process. By maintaining a customer-first approach, you’ll help ensure our products are not only innovative but also deeply relevant and meaningful.

As a product leader, you’ll bring best practices to life in ways that are tailored to HealthVerity’s mission, crafting Data Products that not only address customer pain points but also align with our company’s core values and vision.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Product Management: Develop and execute thoughtful roadmaps for one or more data product areas, aligning with HealthVerity's business objectives while prioritizing customer delight.
  • Product Development: Collaborate with teams across the product lifecycle—from concept to launch—partnering with Data Product Design, Data Product Engineering, and other stakeholders. You’ll also help manage the data product backlog, using Agile methodologies to keep projects on track.
  • Client Engagement: Work closely with our enterprise clients, building relationships to understand their unique challenges and actively incorporating their feedback into our product life cycle to ensure we meet and exceed market needs.
  • Performance Metrics: Track and analyze key performance indicators, helping to measure and enhance the success of our Data Products.
  • Market Research and Insights: Conduct market research to identify opportunities for innovation and enhancement, helping us stay responsive to emerging market needs.
  • Effective Product Launches: Delivering products on time, with high adoption and usability, and meeting roadmap milestones.
  • High Customer Satisfaction: Gathering positive feedback, improving customer retention, and successfully incorporating customer insights into the product.
  • Business Impact: Driving revenue growth through new products or enhancements and helping HealthVerity stand out in the market.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • 3+ years of experience as a product manager for a data centric offering in the healthcare industry
  • Subject matter expertise across various healthcare data types (e.g. claims, EMR, labs, patient-reported outcomes, etc) and coding standards (e.g. ICD, CPT, HCPCS, NDC, LOINC, NUCC taxonomy, etc)
  • Experience in technical data analysis and translating technical concepts, especially in the healthcare space
  • Skills in tools like Excel, SQL, or data visualization platforms (e.g., Tableau, Power BI), as well as foundational models are beneficial
  • Knowledge of the product lifecycle from discovery to launch and beyond
  • Understanding and implementation of product management best practices and principles
  • Familiarity with Agile methodologies (e.g., Scrum or Kanban) and experience collaborating with development teams
  • Exceptional communication and presentation skills that make complex ideas accessible to a diverse audience

Base salary for the role is commensurate with experience and can range between $150,000 - 185,000 + annual bonus opportunity.

Hiring Locations

Our main office is located in Center City, Philadelphia, where we operate on a hybrid model with in-office work required three days a week for local employees. We believe collaboration is most effective when teams come together, which is why we prioritize hiring in the Philadelphia area.

For certain roles, we also hire from hub locations—regions where we have an established presence with multiple team members working remotely. While these employees primarily work from home, we bring them together in person at least once a year for team-building, collaboration, and strategic planning.

Due to tax and labor regulations, we can only hire from specific states. Remote work is supported in the following key hub locations and approved states:

Hub Locations:

  • Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
  • Boston, Massachusetts
  • New York City, New York
  • Baltimore, Maryland
  • Washington, D.C.
  • Charlotte, North Carolina
  • Raleigh-Durham, North Carolina
  • Atlanta, Georgia
  • Chicago, Illinois

Approved States for Remote Work:
CT, DE, FL, GA, IL, IN, MA, MD, MI, NC, NJ, NY, OH, PA, TN, and VA.

About HealthVerity

HealthVerity is the leader in privacy-protected real-world data exchange, transforming how healthcare and life sciences organizations connect and analyze disparate patient data. By enabling access to the industry’s largest RWD ecosystem, HealthVerity supports critical applications in clinical development, commercial strategy, regulatory decision-making, and public health. To learn more about HealthVerity, visit .

Why you'll love working here

We are making a difference – Our technology is at the forefront of some of the biggest healthcare challenges in the world.

We are one team – Our people define our culture and always will. We take time out to celebrate each other, and acknowledge the value that each of us adds towards our greater mission. Come share all you have to offer.

We are learners – Every team member is continually learning, no matter if we've been in a role for one year or much longer. We are committed to learning and implementing what is best for our clients, partners, and each other.

Benefits & Perks

Our benefits package is thoughtfully designed to support and enrich the experience of our full-time employees, with eligibility limited to those in permanent positions.

  • Compensation: competitive base salary & annual bonus opportunity (for non-commissioned roles)
  • Benefits: We offer health, dental, and vision coverage starting on day 1. We also offer a 401(k) plan and an equity program, with new hire equity grants beginning at the Director level and above.
  • Flexible location: Remote workdays and 3 days a week of in-office collaboration for team members in the Philadelphia area. Check location requirements with the recruiting team.
  • Generous PTO: Take time off as needed, targeted at 4 weeks per year, including vacation, personal and sick time, plus paid parental leave.
  • Parental Leave: 12 weeks paid leave for childbearing, surrogacy, and adoption; 6 weeks for non-childbearing parents.
  • Comprehensive and individualized onboarding: mentorship program, departmental talks, and a library of resources are available beginning day 1 for each new team member to minimize the stress of starting a new job
  • Professional development: biweekly 1:1s, hands-on leadership that is goal-and growth-oriented for each team member, and an annual budget to support professional development pursuits

We believe incorporating different ideas, perspectives and backgrounds make us stronger and encourages an environment where ageism, racism, sexism, ableism, homophobia, transphobia or any other form of discrimination are not tolerated. All qualified job applicants will be given consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability. At HealthVerity, we’re working towards an innovative and connected future for healthcare data and believe the future is better together. We can only do that if everyone has a seat at the table.

If you require a reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please direct your inquiries to careers@healthverity.com

Remote opportunities are not available in all areas and require team members to work from a fixed location due to tax and labor law implications - specific questions about remote positions can be discussed during the interview process with your recruiter.

title: Noviam Investment Advisor (Licensed -New York )
description:
Investment Analyst

New York, NY | Full-Time | In-Office | Career-Track


You already know the industry. What you may not have yet is a book of your own.

Most advisory seats hand you someone else's clients and call it a career. This one offers a process and a pathway to grow your own book of business, with your licensing, continuing education, and designations treated as the firm's investment rather than your expense.

At a glance

Location

New York, NY — in-office, five days a week

Experience

0–2 years in financial services

Required licenses

SIE and Series 7

FIRM Sponsored

Series 66, continuing education, CFP® / ChFC® support

Compensation

$60,000 – $80,000 base plus performance bonus

Reports to

Lead Advisor

The role

As a Noviam Investment Advisor, you work alongside a Lead Advisor, service an established book of client relationships, and take on more every quarter, leading client reviews, building pipeline, then carrying your own relationships. The work is real from week one: retirement income, education funding, distribution strategy, the decisions that determine whether a family sleeps at night.

The mix: roughly 70% servicing the existing book, 30% growth at the start, shifting toward growth as you ramp and your own relationships accumulate.

Minimum requirements

These are hard requirements. We review every application that meets them.

Experience

At least 2 years of professional experience in financial services: investment advisory, wealth management, brokerage, or retirement planning, in a client-facing or client-support capacity.

SIE

Required. Securities Industry Essentials exam passed.

Series 7

Required. Active registration, or eligible for reinstatement under FINRA's Maintaining Qualifications Program. Please include your CRD number when you apply.

Series 66

Not required to apply. Sponsored and to be earned within 90 days of hire. Already hold the Series 66, or the 63/65 pair? You skip this step.

Education

Bachelor's degree, or equivalent skills and work experience.

Location

In-office, New York, NY, five days a week. This role is not remote or hybrid.

Eligibility

Authorization to work in the United States and a clean regulatory record. U4 disclosures reviewed case by case.

What you'll do

• Lead client progress reviews, with a Lead Advisor alongside you until you no longer need one.

• Build your own pipeline. Referrals, introductions, seminars, and community engagement are the foundation of the book you'll own.

• Own the meeting cycle. Prepare agendas and materials, run the follow-up, track every relationship's next step so nothing falls through.

• Coordinate with custodians on account opening, transfers, and maintenance, and process service paperwork accurately from start to finish.

• Keep records clean. Detailed, current, and compliant data in CRM and planning software.

• Communicate proactively, so clients never have to chase you for an answer.

• Translate strategy into plain English. The recommendation, the trade-offs, and how their risk tolerance shaped both.

• Show up for the team. Team meetings, seminars, networking events, continuing education.

• Follow our processes — and tell us where they're wrong.

The Noviam pathway

A defined sequence, not a vague promise. Each stage has readiness gates before the next one opens.

1. Onboard

Platform, products, client protocols, and compliance expectations, built around real client scenarios. Shadowing and joint work from the first week.

2. Register

Series 66 preparation with subject-matter-expert instruction, timed practice exams, and clear readiness gates. Sponsored end-to-end: fees, materials, study time.

3. Ramp

You take client reviews with your Lead Advisor, then without. Hands-on coaching, joint work, and honest feedback from people who have built books themselves.

4. Build

Transition to a fully registered Investment Advisor Representative with your own client relationships, the firm's support behind you, and a mentor in your corner.

5. Lead

Our strongest advisors mentor new analysts, then build and run teams of their own as the firm grows. We promote from within: the people who help build the books are the ones who end up running them.

What's in it for you

• Base salary of $60,000 – $80,000 plus performance bonus

• Sponsored Series 66 exam fees, materials, and study support

• Continuing education and licensing maintenance covered

• Support to pursue CFP® and ChFC®

• Health and dental insurance

• PTO plus all holidays off

• Mentorship and joint work with top performers

• A defined path to Investment Advisor Representative, with upside that grows with your own book

What else we look for

• Strong organization, communication, and follow-through are the three things that separate advisors who keep clients from advisors who lose them

• A client-service mindset and genuine coachability, however much experience you arrive with

• Comfort in a structured, fast-paced, accountable environment

• Entrepreneurial drive — you want a book, not a queue

• Experience with CRM and financial planning software

• Prior client-facing experience in a fee-based or hybrid advisory practice (a plus, not a requirement)

Our culture

High-energy and team-first. We work hard, move quickly, and back each other. The people who thrive here share six traits: professionalism, follow-through, positivity, accountability, a growth mindset, and a genuine commitment to taking care of people.

This role is not a fit if…

• You want remote or hybrid. This is five days a week in our New York office.

• You don't hold the SIE and Series 7. If you're early-career and unlicensed, ask about our sponsored entry-level program instead — it exists for exactly that.

• You want to service only, and never prospect. Growth is part of the seat from day one.

• Organization and follow-through aren't your strengths.

• You'd rather not be coached, measured, or held to a process.

• You're looking for a short-term position.

• A fast-paced office environment isn't for you.


Interested?

Applications are welcome at any time — there's no deadline, because we stay open to exceptional people whenever they're ready.

Job type: Full-time, in-office, New York, NY. Compensation: $60,000 – $80,000 base plus performance bonus.

Noviam is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

title: Vice President, Accountnig
description:
Athena Group Advisors

Athena Group Advisors (“Athena”) is the private multi-family office of an investment firm.

Position Overview

Athena is seeking a Vice President (“VP”) of Accounting to support the family office enterprise, our principals, and affiliated non-profit organizations. This role reports to the Director of Tax.

This is a hands-on, outcomes-driven role requiring maniacal attention to detail, focus on consistently delivering high-quality work, and superb follow-through. This role is responsible for managing the end-to-end accounting lifecycle, and requires strong judgment under ambiguity, ability to maintain discretion and confidentiality, creative problem-solving, and the ability to think on your feet.

Key responsibilities:

Individual, Entity, & Investment Accounting

  • Manage individual capital accounts, distributions, and contributions, as needed, for each principal
  • Track and reconcile balance sheets, including illiquid and alternative asset holdings
  • Prepare customized reporting packages reflecting each principal’s unique entity structure and reporting preferences
  • Coordinate with tax, finance, and investment teams to reflect portfolio activity accurately in the books
  • Reconcile investment activity against custodian and administrator statements
  • Account for SPVs created by the family office; manage capital calls, carried interest, and fee calculations. Track ownership percentages and allocations

Financial Reporting & Accounting Operations

  • Prepare and review consolidated and entity-level financial statements across multiple principals’ and their entities, trusts, charitable organizations, and investment vehicles
  • Maintain general ledger integrity across a complex multi-entity chart of accounts (personal, trust, LLC, and SPV structures)
  • Oversee month-end and year-end close processes for the family office enterprise, our principals, and affiliated non-profit organizations
  • Ensure accurate intercompany eliminations and reconciliations across related entities
  • Manage onboarding and offboarding new entities and principals into the accounting infrastructure

Cash Management & Treasury

  • Monitor cash positions across entities and coordinate funding for capital calls, distributions, and personal and entity operating expenses
  • Maintain banking relationships and reconcile multiple bank and custodial accounts
  • Develop, document, and automate cash management and treasury process, leveraging technology where appropriate

Tax Support

  • Support the Director of Tax with K-1 preparation
  • Maintain records necessary for tax compliance across LLCs, trusts, SPVs, and other vehicles
  • Assist with tracking tax basis and other tax attributes tied to investment structures

Compliance & Controls

  • Maintain accounting policies and internal controls consistent with SEC recordkeeping requirements (e.g., Rule 204-2 books and records)
  • Support audit and compliance reviews with organized, audit-ready documentation
  • Ensure segregation of duties and proper approval workflows for disbursements

Other

  • Collaborate with tax, finance, property management, and investments to ensure accurate, timely financial data flows across services lines, providing high-quality service and deliverables to our principals and affiliated organizations
  • Support the Athena leadership team with ad-hoc financial analysis and special projects
  • Maintain and improve accounting systems, workflows, reporting, and templates to scale with growth in principals and entities
  • Document accounting procedures to support consistency
  • Manage third-party vendors (e.g., bookkeepers) that support the accounting and reporting lifecycles and deliverables

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field required. Master’s degree a plus but not required
  • 7-10+ years of relevant experience, ideally at a professional accounting firm, multi-family office, or related environment
  • CPA required; CFP, CFA, or MST a plus but not required
  • Strong knowledge of GAAP and multi-entity/consolidated accounting
  • Experience working across multiple legal entities simultaneously (LLCs, trusts, partnerships, charitable organizations, SPVs)
  • Prior exposure to high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth individuals’ personal financial reporting
  • Experience supporting or working alongside tax, finance, and investment teams in a coordinated service model
  • Familiarity with partnership and trust accounting concepts (capital accounts, allocations, K-1s)
  • Advanced Excel skills; comfort building and maintaining complex reporting templates
  • Experience with accounting software (e.g., Sage Intaact or similar) and family office platforms (e.g., Masttro) a plus
  • High discretion, confidentiality, and data sensitive standards expected in a family office environment
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage competing deadlines across entities and stakeholders
  • Excellent communication skills, comfortable interacting directly with principals and external advisors (accountants, legal, tax professionals)
  • High orientation to detail and accuracy, with low tolerance for reporting errors
  • Adaptability to a growing and evolving organization; collaborative mindset and the ability to work cross-functionally to deliver coordinated, white-glove services

Compensation

The base salary for this New York-based position ranges from $150,000 - $175,000, depending on experience, skills, and responsibilities. Actual salary may vary based on qualifications and the level at which the role is hired. In addition to the base salary, the role includes a discretionary incentive compensation program, and a comprehensive benefits package, including medical and life insurance, retirement plans, tax-free savings options, and access to additional healthcare programs.

As a multi-strategy firm that incorporates fundamental and systematic approaches and emphasizes interdisciplinary analysis, we encourage individuals across a wide breadth of backgrounds to apply. Analysts with a fundamental focus will lead the analysis of companies and industry sectors, analyze and monitor emerging macro-economic and regulatory trends and communicate the impact of these factors on the firm’s investments. Analysts with a quantitative focus will develop systematic trading techniques and/or conduct quantitative research, with an emphasis on alpha signal development, predictive pricing and strategy implementation. All analysts will develop views on company valuation vs. market expectations and relative value across the capital structure and will collaborate with the entire investment team in identifying opportunities to take and manage risk based on your analyses.

In Readystate’s “one team” ethos, you will contribute to a variety of investment styles across convertible bonds, corporate bonds, equities, options and other derivative markets. At Readystate, we foster an environment where all team members can learn from one another and contribute across all aspects of our business, including portfolio management, trading, risk management, operations, technology, and marketing.

Readystate’s Investment Analyst internship offers an immersive introduction to our multi-strategy approach to investing. As an intern, you will rotate through several of our investment strategies, working directly alongside experienced investment professionals generating hypotheses, conducting fundamental and quantitative analysis, and contributing to real investment ideas.

What you can Expect:

  • Direct mentorship from members of our investment team
  • Structured learning sessions and capital markets education throughout the summer
  • Exposure to Readystate's integrated approach, combining fundamental research with quantitative methods
  • A collaborative, transparent culture where every team member's ideas are valued
  • The opportunity to be considered for full-time positions upon graduation

Job Responsibilities:

  • Fundamental due diligence on existing and potential investments, including financial modeling and quantitative assessments of investments
  • Quantitative research/data analysis using market and non-traditional data
  • Idea generation and screening for investment opportunities using fundamental or quantitative techniques
  • Execution of ad hoc projects in collaboration with other team members

Qualifications:

  • A passion for investing and curiosity about financial markets
  • Aptitude to perform fundamental analysis and identify key drivers of value
  • Strong communications skills and the ability to organize and condense unstructured information into a coherent investment thesis
  • Strong analytical skills, the ability to think differently and take initiative
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Python, R, and/or other data analytic tools (higher technical requirements for quantitatively focused analysts)
  • Finance and accounting background are helpful but not required.

Investment Analyst internships are primarily located in our Chicago office, with select opportunities in our New York office.

About Readystate Asset Management

Readystate Asset Management seeks to generate attractive risk adjusted returns through a multi-strategy approach of investing across the capital structure. The firm was founded in 2021 by David Grossman and Ryan Garino, previous co-heads of the Global Credit business at Citadel, and partners for over 15 years. Our fund uses a low beta, relative value framework to construct a diversified portfolio of convertible bond, credit, equity and volatility-based strategies; and believe that risk management is essential at both the investment and portfolio level. Readystate was founded upon a core philosophy to foster and build a culture of integrity, partnership, creative persistence, and excellence.

title: Director of Operations
description:
Alliance Corporation is a leading North American value-added distributor of products and solutions for Wireless Networking, in-building signal coverage and cellular infrastructure applications. We are a fast-paced, aggressive company in an exciting, high-growth market that has shown consistent year-over-year revenue expansion. By partnering with our vendors and clients, we position valued solutions for all of their wireless communications needs.

An exciting career as a Director of Operations in Mississauga, Ontario is available at Alliance!

The Director of Operations leads Alliance Corporation's distribution and logistics network through its site leadership team. The role is based in Mississauga and oversees day-to-day operations at that facility through the Warehouse Manager and carries the same accountability for the Warehouse Managers and daily performance of Alliance's other locations.

The Director owns the operating standards for the network, the KPIs, productivity standards and SOPs that govern how every site runs. They also develop and execute the operations strategy that improves service, expands capability and supports growth.

This role is based at the Alliance Mississauga facility, with regular travel to Alliance's other locations (approximately 25%)

Responsibilities

Leadership and site oversight

  • Lead the Warehouse Managers at all Alliance locations, holding each accountable for the day-to-day performance of their site.
  • Oversee daily operations at Mississauga. On-site presence is necessary for setting direction, resolving escalations and driving change.
  • Work directly with Warehouse Managers and Sales partners to build a culture that promotes involvement, communication, trust and honesty. The role demands a passion for excellence and the willingness to hold staff accountable.
  • Assess existing operations talent, analyze staffing levels, and build a flexible staffing model that improves output and controls labour cost across the network.
  • Provide leadership, coaching and training that raise the capability of the operations and logistics teams and build a bench of site leaders.
  • Manage a geographically distributed team effectively, maintaining standards and visibility at locations the Director does not visit daily.
  • Manage key vendor relationships, ensuring service levels, performance, pricing, and contractual obligations align with organizational needs

Standards, systems and performance

  • Design, implement and own the KPI framework, productivity standards and SOPs that govern operations at every Alliance location, including metric definitions, targets, reporting cadence and the corrective-action process when a site misses.
  • Develop and implement the operations strategy for the network, translating it into site-level plans, sequencing and named accountabilities.
  • Use data and facts to evaluate and communicate site performance; deliver a regular operating review to executive and site leadership.
  • Drive consistency across locations. Where processes differ site to site, decide which standard applies and lead the migration to it.
  • Lead and participate in continuous improvement, technology automation and systems enhancements that improve customer service, increase efficiency or reduce cost.
  • Oversee the receipt, storage and distribution of goods across the network, including inventory accuracy and order fulfillment performance.

Financial accountability

  • Build and manage the operating budget for the locations in scope and hold each site accountable to the budget.
  • Analyze operating and financial reports to identify cost-reduction and efficiency opportunities. Lead the initiatives that capture them without degrading service.

Safety, quality and compliance

  • Ensure every location operates in compliance with the occupational health and safety legislation of its own jurisdiction; Ontario’s OHSA, Alberta’s OHS Act, and federal and state OSHA requirements at the U.S. sites, and that all legal requirements for the operation are adhered to at all times.
  • Ensure each site maintains a functioning health and safety committee, hazard reporting, incident investigation and corrective action, in the form its jurisdiction requires; monitor workers’ compensation claims (WSIB, WCB Alberta, U.S. state programs) and lost-time trends and act on them.
  • Enforce safety and quality standards consistently across the network and lead each location's response to audits and inspections.
  • Lead the organization’s Quality Management System (QMS) and ensure ongoing compliance with ISO90001 standards. Drive a culture of quality and continuous improvement through process oversight, performance measurement, internal audits, and corrective actions

Cross-functional partnership

  • Partner with Sales to align operational capability with customer requirements and service commitments.
  • Work closely with program management to support new initiatives and confirm the operational feasibility of proposed projects.
  • Collaborate across departments to align operating capacity with business growth objectives.
  • Stay current on industry trends, emerging technologies and best practices, and bring the relevant ones into the network.

Core requirements

  • 10+ years leading operations teams, including experience in a distribution or logistics environment.
  • Proven multi-site experience leading through distributed management team, including managing a team remotely across separate time zones.
  • Experience operating a warehouse network that spans provinces and the U.S. states, including differences in employment and safety obligations between them.
  • Demonstrated experience building KPI frameworks, productivity standards and SOPs from the ground up, not solely administering standards set by others.
  • Credibility on the floor: has personally implemented change and new processes in a warehouse environment and can still do so when a site requires it.
  • Experience implementing and training on operations systems and processes; proficiency with WMS and inventory management software.
  • Demonstrated success in staffing and productivity management, and the ability to hold operations staff accountable for running the day-to-day business.
  • Strong customer-service-focused leadership and strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate and build consistency across different locations.
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication and computer skills, and excellent multi-tasking and problem-resolution ability.
  • Working knowledge of Ontario health and safety legislation and employment standards.
  • Bachelor's degree in logistics, supply chain management, business administration or a related field, or equivalent operating experience.

Preferred

  • Experience in a private-equity-backed or multi-entity portfolio environment.
  • Experience leading a WMS implementation or a major systems upgrade.
  • Continuous improvement credentials (Lean, Six Sigma or equivalent).

Compensation: CAD $130,000 - $160,000 annually (plus up to 20% bonus opportunity)

Why Join Our Team?

title: Test Beatrice
description:
Who We Are and What We Do

IMC is a leading global market maker that utilizes algorithmic trading and advanced technology to buy and sell securities across multiple trading venues worldwide. With offices in Amsterdam, Chicago, Sydney, and Mumbai, we provide liquidity to financial markets, driving efficiencies for buyers and sellers.

What You'll Do As a People Analyst Specialist

At IMC, we believe our employees are our greatest asset, and we empower them with responsibility and support to make a difference. As part of our new People Analytics team, your goal will be to leverage our People Data to drive decision-making, supporting our ambitious strategies for the future.

From day one, you will have a broad range of responsibilities and experience a culture that fosters idea-sharing and values quick feedback loops. The team is still young which means you will play a key role in shaping the new journey. As an advisor to HR Leadership and the business, you'll collaborate with team members and key stakeholders to realize strategic analytics initiatives, conduct people research, and experiment to solve critical business and HR challenges. Key focus areas include predicting great hires, turnover, and supporting employee engagement goals.

In this dynamic, fast-paced environment, you'll work with a diverse group of smart individuals, demonstrating strong teamwork, adaptability, and curiosity. As a data-driven People Analytics Specialist, you will thrive on challenges and make a meaningful impact within an international, ambitious, yet informal setting.

Our Technology Stack

Our tech stack includes an ever-evolving range of systems and technologies, and we have the freedom to choose the best solution for each challenge. We actively invest in exploring, adopting, and developing new technologies that add value.

Currently, our team utilizes Python to build and manage data infrastructure, ETLs, and data integrity, ensuring secure data flows across databases and servers in multiple environments like Elastic, AWS, and SQL. You'll also build and enhance existing reporting solutions on Qlik and Python.

Who You Are
  • 3+ years of experience in People Analytics or Analytical Advisory roles
  • BS, MS, or Ph.D. in an analytical/quantitative/psychology-related field of study
  • Excellent analytical, project management and communication skills
  • Experience in data analysis/ visualization using preferably Python, SQL, and Qlik
  • Ability to work successfully in a fast-moving and competitive environment
  • Desire to work in a team environment is a must.

What You Can Expect

Working at IMC means embracing dynamic challenges and a steady stream of diverse projects. Our quick feedback loop allows for continuous improvement and learning. Our workforce is equally diverse, comprising individuals from various nationalities and backgrounds, united by their technical expertise and collaborative approach. We empower our employees to take on significant responsibilities and support them in making an impact from day one. As a People Analytics Specialist, you'll gain insights into all aspects of our work, making your job even more exciting and fulfilling.

We offer a flat organizational structure and a collaborative culture that fosters idea-sharing and technology exchange between teams and offices. You'll have opportunities to travel between offices and explore different parts of our organization. Traveling required approx. 15%.

Our Hiring Process

For your success, we've detailed our hiring process, including tips on applying and interviewing with us, on our website. Now it's your turn! Apply today to embark on an amazing journey with IMC.

IMC: Join a World-Class Global Market Maker

IMC is a world-renowned market maker with offices in Europe, the US and Asia-Pacific. We use algorithmic trading and advanced technology to buy and sell securities across multiple trading venues. Our vital role, at the centre of the financial markets, provides liquidity for buyers and sellers worldwide.

In the late 1980s, IMC quickly identified the importance of technology in the fast-evolving trading environment. Our passion for innovation continues to drive us today. Although our company has grown rapidly over recent decades, we still approach our work with the same entrepreneurial spirit, with an emphasis on continuous improvement and innovation. We like our people to think for themselves and we give them the responsibility and support they need to make an impact. This means real work as well as dedicated training programmes and mentors.

While we work hard, we also have a lot of fun – whether solving complex problems or taking part in team-building, leisure and sporting activities. IMC also enables its employees to contribute to a better society through our foundation.

title: DVM Student Externship/Preceptorship Program - Coldwater Animal Hospital
description:
We're making an investment in the next generation of veterinary doctors!

As part of the professional veterinary curriculum, colleges encourage off-campus educational experiences in practices outside of the teaching hospital. Practical experience in a well-run and contemporary practice can be a valuable component of your veterinary education, preparing you to deliver better care after graduation. Our program is dedicated to contributing to your practice-readiness and to help you hit the ground running after graduation.

Our program structure:

Our externships are flexible—they can range from two to eight weeks during the year, according to your college curriculum – but are typically two or three weeks in length. Your schedule will include days, evenings and weekends.

Our externship rotations are designed to allow students, under veterinary supervision, to practice the problem-solving, technical and communication skills that they have acquired during their clinical preparation. Externs are given the opportunity to work alongside our veterinary team and are encouraged to participate in all aspects of patient care. A stipend of $250 per week will be provided.

What you'll be doing:

Externs experience the typical caseload of a small animal practice. Under the supervision of your mentor doctor you will gather histories, perform physical examinations, develop diagnostic and therapeutic plans, scrub in to surgery, assist in the management of medical cases, provide wellness care, develop your client communication skills, polish your technical skills and produce appropriate medical records (SOAPs) within the time limits of daily practice.

Who we're looking for:

Extern students are expected to be enthusiastic and effective participants in our patient care activities, upholding the professional and ethical standards of our practice. Students participating in the externship program are suggested to review the Veterinary Practice Act in regard to the scope of duties that may be performed, and to be familiar with the type and degree of veterinary supervision that is required. These should be followed carefully in order to protect both yourself and our practice.

As a veterinary student extern, we expect you to dress and behave in a professional manner and to meet the expectations that we have of all team members as outlined in our employee handbook.

Requirements:

  • Be enrolled in an accredited DVM program.
  • You are authorized to work in the United States.
  • You must carry professional liability insurance. AVMA PLIT liability insurance is free for all student members of the AVMA. You may apply for this coverage on their website. Please check to make sure your coverage is current and submit a certificate of coverage with your application.

About us:

As sponsors of the Veterinary Externship Program, we see ourselves to be part of your educational team, providing instruction, mentoring and evaluation of the students who participate. You will be assigned a mentor and work on the learning objectives as defined by your college program or to meet your specific goals. At the end of the externship your mentor will provide a written evaluation of your performance as required by your college program.

We look forward to working with you!

  • Monitor project costs against estimates and identify and address potential cost overruns.

  • Manage subcontractor performance, including scope, schedule, coordination, change orders, invoicing, and issue resolution.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients and provide regular communication regarding project progress, risks, changes, and upcoming activities.

  • Coach and develop project team members while establishing clear roles, responsibilities, and performance expectations.
  • Support project closeout and ensure systems, equipment, documentation, and deliverables are completed in accordance with project requirements.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of construction project management, project engineering, or related field construction experience.
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Experience supporting or managing large, complex construction projects, preferably $20M+.
  • Strong understanding of construction means and methods, sequencing, field operations, and subcontractor coordination.
  • Experience managing project budgets, estimates, forecasts, cost reports, and financial performance.
  • Experience developing and managing construction schedules and critical-path activities.
  • Demonstrated experience with change orders, project risk, claims documentation, and contract administration.

  • Strong understanding of construction safety, quality, and regulatory requirements.
  • Ability to effectively manage multiple project priorities and communicate with field teams, clients, subcontractors, and senior leadership.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience directing and developing construction project teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • You'll set the technical direction. Make the big architectural calls across our ecosystem and live with the consequences. The kind of decisions that are easy to get wrong early and expensive to fix later. You'll make them with conviction because you've made them before.
  • You'll solve the problems no one's solved yet. Offline-first healthcare, real-time clinical audio transcription, private AI compute, and graphs all the way down. In environments where nothing works the way it should. There's no playbook for what we're building. You'll write it.
  • You'll define how we build, not just what we ship. We don't think AI is a feature we ship. It's how we build. You'll design the workflows, tooling, and automation that let a team of four operate like a team of forty. This is as core to the role as anything you'll put in production.
  • You'll ship it with us. Work directly with co-founders and clinicians across the full stack, from API design to mobile recording flows to the interfaces patients and caregivers actually use. You'll feel the weight of that and love it.

What we're looking for

We're building for people navigating the scariest moments of their lives. That shapes everything about who we hire, how we build, and what we ship.

  • You've seen what good looks like. You've shipped software people depend on in messy, unpredictable environments and you came out the other side with opinions. About failure modes, about schema design, about what holds up at scale and what quietly falls apart. Healthcare data raises the bar on all of it, not just compliance, but the deeper constraints that come from earning and keeping patient trust.
  • The tools change. You don't. We care about how you think through problems, not which frameworks you've memorized. Our stack is Hono, React Native/Expo, React, and PostgreSQL, all TypeScript end to end. You'll pick up the specifics. What stays constant is the judgment, knowing which tradeoff to make when there are six reasonable options and real urgency behind all of them.
  • You've already rewired how you build. You use LLMs and agentic tools in your actual day to day, not as experiments. You have real opinions about where they help and where they get in the way. You're excited to help a small team define what AI-assisted development looks like when it's not a buzzword but a genuine advantage.
  • Everyone gets better when you show up. You leave behind clear patterns that make the next decision easier. You write things down. You make complex tradeoffs feel obvious in retrospect. The best engineers you've worked with did this for you, and now you do it for others.

How we work

1. Patient-First Obsession

The North Star. When in doubt, ask whose interests this serves. We build for the person at the end of the care chain, not for the roadmap, not for the demo, not for the investor. When patient outcomes and internal convenience conflict, patient outcomes win. Every time.

2. No Silos, No Heroes

Empowerment over Dependency. We operate with radical transparency and assume positive intent, empowering each other to take ownership and challenge ideas rather than people.

3. Magic in Simplicity

Earn Complexity. Simple until it has to be otherwise. We ship to learn, cut scope to move, and resist the urge to architect for problems we don't have yet. Complexity is a cost. We only pay it when the return is clear.

4. Sustainable Intensity

Energy over Hours.

Energy is the asset, not hours. We bring full force when it matters and protect recovery because burnout doesn't serve patients. Intensity is a tool we choose.

Hybrid in Los Angeles, CA

Compensation and equity

This role includes a competitive salary, meaningful equity, and benefits. Our offers reflect job scope, location, and relevant experience.

title: Senior AI Payment Agent Engineer
description:
Our Client

Our client is an established global fintech organisation helping banks and financial institutions modernise their platforms and connect to blockchain-based payments and settlement.

This position focuses on building the technical foundation for payment-capable AI agents. You will design and own the systems that unify LLMs, agent orchestration frameworks, legacy payment rails, and blockchain infrastructure, supporting autonomous machine-to-machine payments, self-pay API access, and automated cross-border financial workflows as the company scales its AI workforce products for commercial use.

In this role, you will:

  • Build AI agents: Design and deploy production-ready autonomous AI agents and Digital FTEs with reasoning, planning, and multi-step workflow capabilities, optimizing multi-agent collaboration with frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or OpenClaw.
  • Architect payment systems: Own end-to-end architecture for AI payments, cross-border acquiring, clearing, and hybrid on-chain/off-chain settlement, integrating payment gateways and Web3 stacks, including stablecoin settlement and the x402 protocol.
  • Standardise agent payment frameworks: Establish reusable frameworks, plugins, and toolkits for agent invocation, transaction execution, permission governance, and error fallback logic across multi-agent payment scenarios.
  • Ensure compliance and reliability: Apply guardrails, budget caps, approval pipelines, and cryptographic signatures so autonomous transactions stay deterministic, auditable, and regulation-compliant.
  • Maintain production stability: Optimise system performance, capacity, and security, resolve critical incidents, and maintain 24/7 uninterrupted service.

You'll be a great fit if you have:

  • Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Software Engineering, AI, or a related field.
  • 3+ years building backend architectures and distributed systems, with hands-on experience developing LLMs and AI agents.
  • Strong backend development skills in Go or Java, with proficiency in Python or TypeScript/Node.js.
  • Deep expertise in microservices, distributed transactions, message queues, caching, and database sharding.
  • Practical experience with agent frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or AutoGen.
  • Familiarity with RESTful APIs, OpenAPI specs, and function calling for GPT, Claude, and Gemini.
  • A track record of taking AI products from prototype to production, including prompt evaluation, tracing, and latency optimization.
  • Fluent English for reviewing technical documentation and daily collaboration.

Nice to have:

  • Deep knowledge of the x402 protocol and machine-to-machine payment architecture.
  • Experience launching Digital FTE or AI workforce platforms.
  • Familiarity with Panaversity Agentic AI technologies (OpenWork, Cowork, OpenClaw, Loop Engineering).
  • Hands-on experience with cloud AI infrastructure such as AWS Bedrock AgentCore or Google Vertex AI.

title: Lead Polisher
description:

title: Part Time Gym Operations
description:
Momentum is seeking enthusiastic and outgoing applicants for the Gym Operations positions at our SoDo, Seattle location. This customer-focused position includes the majority of tasks required to run the gym on a day-to-day basis. Gym Operations staff provide a diverse range of services to our customers including, but not limited to, sales, membership maintenance, risk mitigation, opening and closing, and cleaning.

title: On-Site Safety Supervisor
description:
The On-Site Safety Supervisor plays a pivotal role in ensuring that safety and quality control standards are upheld across various job sites. This entry-level to mid-level position requires extensive travel to job sites, most of which are out of state. All travel and lodging expenses are fully covered by the company.

This role involves conducting safety inspections, issuing reports, overseeing the proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and tools, delivering weekly toolbox talks, and prioritizing crew members' well-being. This individual will be assigned to a project and will be stationed there for several months. The Safety Supervisor must exhibit strong leadership skills, attention to detail, and a commitment to maintaining a safe work environment.

This is a full-time role eligible for overtime. Extensive travel is expected for this position. Most job sites are located outside GA, and all travel and lodging expenses are fully covered by the company. Up to 30 days of travel is expected for candidates based in GA.

Hourly Pay: $20.00-$25.00/hour

Duties and Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Travel to Job Sites: This position entails significant travel, with a 30-day rotation schedule outside the state, followed by 3-5 days off between rotations to ensure adequate rest and recovery. This role involves assignments on projects lasting up to 6 months.
  • Safety Inspections: Conduct thorough inspections of work areas, equipment, and practices to identify potential hazards or safety concerns. Take necessary steps to mitigate risks and address issues promptly.
  • Send Report: Compile detailed reports on safety observations, incidents, and corrective actions. Communicate findings to relevant stakeholders and management promptly.
  • Quality Control: Collaborate with project managers and supervisors to maintain high standards of workmanship and quality in roofing projects. Implement measures to address any deficiencies identified.
  • PPE and Tool Inspection: Monitor the availability, condition, and proper usage of personal protective equipment and tools. Ensure all equipment meets safety standards and is maintained appropriately.
  • Toolbox Talks: Organize and lead weekly toolbox talks or safety meetings to discuss relevant topics, share best practices, and reinforce safety protocols among crew members.
  • Driving Company Vehicle: Safely operate a company vehicle to travel between job sites and perform job duties. Maintain the vehicle in a clean and functional condition, adhering to all traffic laws and regulations.
  • Crew Well-Being: Act as a resource and advocate for the well-being of crew members. Address any concerns related to safety, health, or working conditions promptly and empathetically.

Minimum Employment Requirements:

  • Clear a National, State, and Local Background Check
  • 3-Year Motor Vehicle Record meets standards for driving company vehicles; have a current & valid Driver's License
  • Candidates must pass a pre-employment drug screen & physical
  • Pass the 90-day introductory period
  • Must be willing to travel for up to 30 days
  • Computer-savvy; have experience with Google Workspace, Slack & safety platforms such as ClickSafety & Mitti (SafetyCulture)

Qualifications:

  • Certification in Occupational Health and Safety (e.g., OSHA 30-hour Construction Safety) is preferred but not required
  • 40-60 Hour Work Weeks with up to 100% Travel
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively convey safety information and instructions
  • Strong organizational abilities and attention to detail, with the capacity to manage multiple tasks and priorities
  • Leadership qualities, including the ability to motivate and influence others to prioritize safety
  • Periodic, Regional, and overnight stays for job completion
  • Physical fitness and ability to work in various weather conditions and environments
  • Commitment to continuous learning and professional development in safety practices and Previous experience installing Metal Accessories: Gutters, Downspouts, Fascia, Coping, Drip Edge, etc., in accordance with regulations.
  • Ability to install the following Roofing Systems; TPO, PVC, Modified Bitumen, Fully Adhered, Mechanically Attached, Rhinobond, etc.

The On-Site Safety Supervisor plays a vital role in promoting a culture of safety and excellence within the organization, contributing to the success of roofing projects while prioritizing the well-being of all personnel involved. Training for this position will be 1-2 weeks in the office, depending on existing certifications & experience.

Benefits:

  • Weekly Paychecks
  • Paid vacation and holidays.
    • Extra Holidays Paid: New Years Eve, Christmas Eve, and Friday after Thanksgiving
  • 401K Plan with Company Match.
  • Generous Referral Bonus Program
  • Work / Home Life Balance.
  • Industry Leading safe working conditions.
  • Ongoing safety training and performance enhancement.

Work Environment:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to fumes or airborne particles, moving mechanical parts, and vibration. The employee is occasionally exposed to a variety of extreme conditions at roofing job sites. The weather, work environment, and job sites can be extremely hot or extremely cold. This position is performed inside and outside.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that an employee must meet to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Travel:

title: Senior Software Architect
description:
Who We Are


Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.


What We Offer


Location:

Rehovot,ISR

You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.

As a Software Engineer at Applied Materials, you’ll dive deep into ground-breaking technologies—like machine learning and AI—to craft novel software solutions that solve our customers’ high-value problems. Our Software Engineers are responsible for designing, prototyping, developing, and debugging software solutions for semiconductor equipment components and devices to ensure quality and functionality. You'll develop software documentation and test procedures, troubleshoot software problems, and communicate with internal customers to understand project requirements. As part of our team, you'll contribute your expertise in intricate systems, deciphering code, and anticipating software behaviors to ensure Applied remains the leader in the semiconductor and display sectors.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Software Architect to join our dynamic team. As a Senior Software Architect, you will own the architecture of large-scale, data-dense frontend systems, designing solutions that align with our organization's strategic goals. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, including developers, algorithm developers, engineers, and product managers, to deliver a frontend architecture that scales across teams and meets the needs of our clients.

What's in it for you?

As a Software Frontend Architect, you will have:

  • The responsibility to design a platform used across teams, drive its adoption, and mentor engineers along the way.

  • Be a key player in the architecture of one of the most data-dense, real-time systems we build, employing state-of-the-art technology.

  • Opportunities for professional development and career advancement.

  • Work on cutting-edge rendering, real-time, and visualization technologies.

  • A collaborative and inclusive work environment where your architectural decisions are valued.

Our Group — Responsible for the two leading Sophisticated Scanning Electron Microscopes (SEM).

  • Build and maintain the costumer software that autonomously controls and operates a state-of-the-art, nano-resolution Scanning Electron Microscope system.

  • Composed of strong individuals, empowered, service-minded SW engineers.

  • Driven from business value, enable & partner with product teams.

Key responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end frontend architecture for one or more SEM domains — client applications, shared UI infrastructure, rendering, and real-time data flows.

  • Design and evolve large, complex frontend architectures built on React, TypeScript, and Redux, with deep expertise in rendering behavior and performance characteristics at scale.

  • Design a platform or framework from scratch and drive its adoption across teams you do not manage.

  • Architect and operate a micro-frontend ecosystem using Module Federation — defining boundaries, managing shared dependencies and versioning, and enabling independent deployment.

  • Own application state management strategy at scale across a distributed frontend.

  • Design and optimize data-dense, continuously updating UIs — canvas/WebGL or image rendering, large grids, and visualization — backed by real-time transports (WebSocket/SSE).

  • Understand and influence the full data flow, from backend services through real-time transports to rendering, making architectural decisions that hold up across the entire stack, not just on the client.

  • Collaborate closely with backend and algorithm teams on API design, data contracts, and performance trade-offs that affect both ends of the system.

  • Bring enough backend/system-design fluency to evaluate where logic and state should live, spot cross-stack bottlenecks, and challenge or validate architectural decisions outside the frontend when needed.

  • Lead frontend performance engineering: profiling, measurement, performance budgets, and concrete optimization work.

  • Make architectural decisions that account for real constraints — domain model, team topology, release cadence, and legacy footprint.

  • Establish architectural governance and guardrails (design reviews, standards, reference patterns) that keep frontend quality consistent, including for AI-assisted development.

  • Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues as they arise, across both frontend and backend touchpoints.

  • Mentor engineers and architects; grow a frontend architecture community of practice — and be ready to speak credibly to backend architecture and distributed system trade-offs in technical interviews and design reviews, even though day-to-day ownership is frontend-focused.

What you will need

  • 10+ years in software engineering, with 5+ years in architecture roles for web clients.

  • Deep expertise with React, Angular or VueJS, TypeScript, State-Management libs including rendering behavior and performance characteristics at scale.

  • Proven experience designing large, complex frontend architectures.

  • Mastery of application state management at scale.

  • Solid working knowledge of backend architecture and system design (APIs, services, data modeling, distributed systems) —you should be able to design, debug, and reason about it credibly.

  • Hands-on production experience with micro-frontends and Module Federation.

  • A track record of designing a platform or framework from scratch and driving its adoption across teams you did not manage.

  • Experience with data-dense, canvas/WebGL visualization — and with real-time transports in the browser.

  • Strong frontend performance engineering: profiling, measurement, budgets, and concrete optimization.

  • The ability to design around real constraints — domain model, team topology, release cadence, legacy footprint.

Who we are?

Applied Materials Israel is home to the Process Diagnostics and Control business unit (PDC). Based in Rehovot, we develop, manufacture and market cutting-edge machine learning and computer vision-based metrology and inspection products that are essential elements in wafer fabrication. By playing a significant role in enabling the production of the next generation of microchips, our expertise enables our customers to transform possibilities into reality.

Additional Information

Time Type:

Full time

Employee Type:

Assignee / Regular

Travel:

Not Specified

Relocation Eligible:

No

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, citizenship, ancestry, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

As Canada's first and only regulated digital asset custodian, we've built the institutional foundation the market now demands. We're backed by Urbana Corporation, National Bank, ATB Financial, Wealthsimple, Purpose Unlimited, Shakepay, Shopify, and Coinbase Ventures — some of the most consequential names in Canadian finance and fintech.

We operate two interconnected businesses: Tetra Trust, our regulated custody arm and CADD, a compliant on-chain payment rail backed 1:1 by Canadian dollars.

In May 2026, we launched CADD — Canada's first CAD-backed stablecoin issued by a regulated financial institution — following approval from Alberta Treasury Board and Finance. It's live on Base, Ethereum, and Tempo today, with Solana next. CoinDesk and BNN Bloomberg covered it as the arrival of Canada's first regulated digital dollar.

Here’s the problem we’re actually solving: Canada clears roughly $424 billion every business day, and much of the retail payment infrastructure underneath it was designed in the 1980s. Batch windows. Cut-off times. Weekends off. We're the team replacing that with rails that settle continuously, programmatically, and under real regulatory oversight.

We're a team of under 30. The infrastructure we've built punches well above that number, and so does the opportunity ahead.

You own the ground everything else stands on.

Custody doesn't get a maintenance window. Neither does a payment rail. When a Canadian bank settles CADD at 2am or an asset manager needs proof of holdings before a board meeting, our platform is either up and provably correct or we have a very different kind of morning.

This is a genuine platform ownership role, not a ticket queue. You'll define how we build, deploy, observe, secure, and recover — and you'll do it inside a licensed trust company, which means your infrastructure decisions become audit artifacts and client diligence answers. Terraform that gets read by an auditor hits differently than Terraform that gets read by nobody.

Here’s the edge, stated plainly: in this industry, an infrastructure failure isn't downtime, it’s a headline. The graveyard of crypto companies that got custody, key handling, or access control wrong is public, permanent, and instructive. We intend to stay out of it, and we're hiring the person who helps guarantee that.

You’ll report to (Head of Engineering / CTO) and partner closely with our security, compliance, and operations leads.

What You’ll Own

  • Infrastructure as code, end to end. (AWS) estates, (Terraform), environment parity, and the unglamorous discipline of making sure nothing important exists only because someone once clicked it.
  • CI/CD and deployment safety. Pipelines that make shipping routine and make a bad ship hard. Progressive rollout, fast rollback, meaningful gates.
  • Observability and incident response. Metrics, logs, traces, alerts that mean something at 3am, runbooks a tired human can follow, and blameless postmortems we actually act on.
  • Secrets, access, and key material boundaries. Working alongside security on (KMS/HSM/Vault), least-privilege IAM, credential rotation, and the operational envelope around signing infrastructure.
  • Controls that constrain you, too. We’re a custodian, so segregation of duties is real. You’ll help design peer approval, break‑glass procedures, and immutable audit logging — including for your own access. If that sounds like a loss of power rather than a mark of a serious platform, this isn’t your role.
  • Resilience and DR. Backup, restore, failover, and the tested confidence that we can bring it all back. Untested DR is a rumour.
  • Compliance evidence, automated. SOC 2‑style control evidence generated by the system instead of assembled by a human in a spreadsheet the week before an audit.

What We’re Looking For

  • 6+ years in DevOps, SRE, platform, or cloud infrastructure engineering, including production ownership of systems where failure had real consequences
  • Deep (AWS) (or equivalent cloud) — networking, IAM, multi‑account architecture, and the cost side of the house
  • Fluent in infrastructure as code. (Terraform) as a first language, not a copy‑paste ritual
  • Container orchestration — (Kubernetes/ECS) in anger, not in a tutorial
  • Real secrets and identity management experience. You know why “it's in an environment variable” isn't an answer
  • Incident maturity. You’ve been the one on the bridge, you’ve written the postmortem, and you’ve shipped the fix that made that class of failure impossible
  • You write code. Not necessarily application features, but scripting and tooling that other engineers rely on
  • Communication under pressure. You can explain an outage to a compliance officer and a client without either of them feeling managed

Crypto experience is a plus, not a requirement

  • You've been through SOC 2 Type II, PCI, OSFI‑adjacent, or provincial regulatory examination and lived
  • Experience with node infrastructure, MPC, or hardware security modules
  • You've built a platform that a small team could operate — force multiplication over cleverness
  • You have a strong, specific opinion about alert fatigue and you're right

What You Get

  • 200,000–300,000 base salary, commensurate with experience
  • Comprehensive health, dental, and paramedical coverage
  • 1,000 annual learning budget for cloud and security certifications, courses, and conferences
  • Hybrid Toronto — With real flexibility around it
  • Generous vacation, and the cultural expectation that you actually take it
  • A front‑row seat to Canada’s digital asset transformation — this is a rare opportunity to be part of something that doesn’t exist yet
  • A small, high‑calibre team where your work is visible, your contributions are felt, and your growth is real

Tetra moves fast and the expectations are high. We're not a place that slows down to accommodate bureaucracy or process for its own sake. But we're also a licensed trust company, and some things genuinely cannot break. Holding both of those at once is the actual skill.

Some honest specifics, because you'll ask in the interview anyway and we'd rather answer now:

  • On-call is real and it's shared. 24/7 market, 24/7 platform, we protect recovery time, and we are explicitly hiring toward a bigger rotation rather than one hero with a phone.
  • You’ll inherit some things you didn't build. We're five years in and pragmatic. There is work to clean up, and we'd rather you see it in week one than week ten.
  • You will not be a solo function forever. Platform is on the hiring roadmap beyond this role. If you want to eventually lead it, say so in your application — that's a conversation we're happy to have.
  • You’ll be building controls, not just capability. Roughly some of this job is enabling engineers to ship, and some of it is making sure nobody, including you, can do something irreversible alone. Both matter.

If you've spent your career waiting for a fully defined job description before getting started, this isn't the right fit. But if you see a gap and fill it, thrive in ambiguity, and take real ownership of outcomes, this role was built for you.

Tetra is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply and will provide accommodation throughout the hiring process upon request.

In a world of noise, we find the signal — the pulse of potential. We weave the strands of talent, vision, and purpose into organizations that endure. Blending intelligence with intuition, we honor the human art of connection at the heart of every great company.

About the Job

We are partnered with a global consumer brand on the search for its next SVP of Product / Chief Product Officer. This is a mission-critical executive role with broad enterprise impact, reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a core member of the executive leadership team.

The company is at an inflection point—scaling globally, expanding its portfolio, and redefining how product strategy, innovation, and execution come together across hardware, software, and ecosystem experiences.

This leader will be responsible for shaping the end-to-end product vision while ensuring disciplined execution, commercial relevance, and operational excellence at scale.

The Mandate

This organization is very clear about what it is—and is not—seeking.

They are not looking for a purely conceptual product leader or someone focused only on long-range vision without accountability to delivery, margin, or market performance.

They are seeking a builder–operator: a product executive who can set a clear product north star, translate strategy into shipped products, and align engineering, design, supply chain, marketing, and sales around a cohesive roadmap that drives growth and differentiation.

  • Proven track record shipping successful consumer products at scale
  • Deep understanding of product management, user-centered design, and engineering collaboration
  • Experience operating at the intersection of hardware, software, and ecosystem services strongly preferred
  • Commercially grounded: understands margin, cost structures, and go-to-market realities

This is a hands-on technical leadership role for an experienced engineer who combines strong software engineering fundamentals with practical machine learning expertise. You will work on production systems where scalability, accuracy, speed, reliability, and operational efficiency are critical.

You will take end-to-end ownership of machine learning solutions, from system and pipeline design through deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

  • Design, develop, test, and deploy reusable libraries, frameworks, services, and core machine learning infrastructure.
  • Build systems that enable machine learning models to be deployed and operated reliably at scale.
  • Work closely with product managers, machine learning practitioners, data teams, and software engineers to translate business problems into practical technical solutions.

Qualifications

Experience/Requirements:

  • Strong background in digital and mixed-signal hardware design.
  • Experience developing processor-based systems including memory, power management, charging, and high-speed interfaces.
  • Experience with LPDDR4/LPDDR5, USB, PCIe, Ethernet, and battery-powered embedded products.
  • Strong understanding of low-power design techniques and power management architectures.
  • Experience supporting high-volume commercial product development from concept through production.
  • Knowledge of signal integrity, power integrity, EMI/EMC, and PCB layout best practices.
  • Strong board-level troubleshooting and lab debugging skills.
  • Working knowledge of LTE, 5G, Wi-Fi, or other wireless communication products.
