Our team combines technical expertise, business understanding, and a commitment to quality to deliver effective solutions and build lasting client relationships based on responsiveness, consistency, and results.

Forward Deployed Engineer

Full-time, permanent | Remote-first

🎯 Role Overview

We are hiring builders, not tool users. A Forward Deployed Engineer at EVOCS is one person who can sit with a business stakeholder, understand the problem, decompose it into a workflow-based solution, select the right technology, and build a working prototype — typically within one to two days — then hand it to a delivery team and move to the next problem.

Your output is a workforce multiplier: you build the tool and hand it to someone else so they can do something they otherwise never could. You are not the long-term user or operator of what you build.

We are an AI-native firm: we build our own tooling, automate our own operations, and hold our client work to the same standard.

🧩 What You Will Do

  • Solution. Sit with business owners, understand inputs and required outcomes, and decompose ambiguous problems into buildable, workflow-based solutions on the spot.
  • Prototype. Build working prototypes fast — automations, integrations, internal applications — test them against a limited scope, and validate with the actual users within days, not weeks.
  • Hand off. Document the solution, hand it to delivery managers and delivery teams for productionization and rollout, then move on.
  • Internal platform work. Build and improve EVOCS's own back office: internal automations, auditing tools, reporting, and integrations across our HR, finance, PM, and IT systems.
  • Escalation SWAT. Act as rapid-response technical firepower on client escalations — diagnose the actual error, design the fix, and give the delivery team a concrete build plan within hours.
  • Pre-sales support. Contribute solution designs and technical approaches to RFP responses and client proposals when the pipeline needs them.

🧠 What You Will Bring

  • Full-stack proficiency: you can independently design, build, and ship an end-to-end solution — front end, back end, integration, and data layer.
  • Deep data literacy: data modeling, transformation, and migration; you know when a problem calls for a relational store, a NoSQL/document store, or an immutable event log, and can defend the choice.
  • Cloud infrastructure fluency (Azure and/or AWS): you can stand up, secure, and connect the services your solution needs.
  • Business decomposition skills: you can take a vague, high-level problem and break it into requirements, workflows, states, and edge cases without a business analyst doing it for you.
  • AI-native working style: you use modern AI tooling to compress work that used to take months (data wrangling, scaffolding, documentation) into hours — and you can build and repair your own harnesses when they break.
  • Judgment for the audience: you build simple. Solutions must work for non-technical users, not just for engineers.
  • 7+ years across software engineering, integration, or solution architecture roles, with a track record of shipping under time pressure.

🚫 What This Role Is Not

  • Not a project manager or delivery owner. Delivery managers own client relationships, escalation politics, resourcing, and margin.
  • Not a low-code-only operator. Off-the-shelf automation tools have their place, but if that is the ceiling of your toolkit, this is not the right role.
  • Not the long-term operator of what you build. You prototype, prove it, document it, hand it over, and move to the next problem.

🛠️ Show Us What You Build

The people who are strong in this role tend to have built things nobody asked them for. That evidence counts here, and it often counts more than what is on the resume.

  • Something you built end to end and shipped: front end, back end, integration, data.
  • An automation or internal tool you wrote because something annoyed you.
  • A prototype you turned around in days that changed what someone else was able to do.
  • A GitHub profile, a demo, a technical writeup, or a harness you built and then repaired when it broke.

Send links. Something working that we can look at will get you further with us than another certification.

⭐ What Will Make You Stand Out

  • Consulting or professional services delivery experience, building under client time pressure.
  • Integration and iPaaS depth, and familiarity with the enterprise systems we touch: HR, finance, PM, and ITSM platforms.
  • Experience building on top of LLM APIs: agents, tool harnesses, retrieval, and evaluation.
  • Data migration at scale, including the cleanup nobody scoped for.
  • Azure or AWS certification — useful, though never a substitute for what you have built.
  • Experience working across distributed delivery teams and multiple time zones.
  • Working Spanish, given our Argentina delivery hub.

🤝 How We Will Work Together

You report to the Chief Technology Officer. You are the front of the wedge: you prove the solution works, then delivery teams productionize and roll it out.

Delivery managers own the client relationship, escalation politics, resourcing, and margin. You own the build and whether it actually solves the problem. That line is deliberate, and it holds.

You will work alongside our Solution Architects, who design at the enterprise level while you prove the critical path in code.

Expect to move between a client escalation, internal platform work, and pre-sales support in the same week. If you want to sit inside one codebase for a year, this is the wrong role.

title: BEVERLY - UNARMED DL
description:
Position Summary

The Public Safety Officer is a hands-on security and safety position responsible for maintaining a safe, secure, and welcoming environment for employees, visitors, residents, guests, property, and company assets.

The Public Safety Officer performs duties including access control and completing detailed security reports.

This position requires a professional and highly visible presence, strong situational awareness, excellent communication skills, and the ability to respond appropriately to routine security concerns, safety issues, and emergency situations.

Primary Public Safety Responsibilities

  • Maintain a professional, highly visible, and approachable public safety presence throughout the assigned property.
  • Monitor entrances and exits
  • Identify and report suspicious persons, vehicles, activity, safety hazards, property damage, unsecured doors, and other security or safety concerns.
  • Monitor access to the property and ensure only authorized individuals enter controlled or restricted areas.
  • Verify identification, credentials, visitor authorization, or access permissions when required.
  • Maintain visitor, contractor, vendor, delivery, and other required access logs.
  • Assist employees, visitors, residents, guests, and members of the public in a professional and courteous manner.
  • Provide directions and general assistance while maintaining appropriate safety and security awareness.
  • Enforce property rules, policies, post orders, and safety procedures professionally and respectfully.
  • Use communication and de-escalation techniques whenever appropriate to resolve situations safely.
  • Immediately notify management, law enforcement, fire departments, EMS, or other emergency services when circumstances require escalation.
  • Preserve incident scenes and protect evidence when appropriate until management or emergency responders arrive.
  • Never exceed assigned authority or engage in unnecessary physical confrontation.
  • Complete detailed Daily Activity Reports.
  • Complete incident reports whenever required.
  • Documenting safety hazards, maintenance concerns, property damage, and suspicious activity.
  • Completing reports before the end of the assigned shift whenever possible.
  • Immediately communicating serious incidents or urgent concerns to management.

Professional Conduct

Public Safety Officers are expected to maintain a high level of professionalism at all times.

Officers must:

  • Arrive on time, properly uniformed, and ready for duty.
  • Maintain a clean and professional appearance.
  • Remain alert and attentive throughout the entire shift.
  • Remain at the assigned post or patrol area unless properly relieved or directed otherwise.
  • Treat all individuals professionally, respectfully, and impartially.
  • Avoid unnecessary personal cell phone use and other distractions while on duty.
  • Maintain confidentiality regarding security operations, incidents, client information, access procedures, and other sensitive information.
  • Follow all company policies, site-specific post orders, safety procedures, and lawful management instructions.
  • Never sleep while on duty.
  • Never abandon an assigned post.
  • Never leave the property without proper authorization or relief.

Qualifications

Required:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Previous security, public safety, military, law enforcement, customer service, or related experience preferred.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to write clear, accurate, and detailed reports.
  • Strong observation and situational-awareness skills.
  • Ability to remain calm and make sound decisions during emergencies.
  • Ability to interact professionally with employees, visitors, residents, guests, and members of the public.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Reliable attendance and punctuality.
  • Ability to understand and follow written post orders and verbal instructions.

Preferred Certifications:

  • First Aid/CPR/AED
  • Narcan/Opioid Overdose Response
  • Crowd Management
  • De-escalation or Crisis Response Training
  • Other applicable state or site-specific security/public safety certifications

Physical & Working Requirements

  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods.
  • Ability to conduct interior and exterior patrols in varying weather conditions.
  • Ability to climb stairs and access designated patrol locations.
  • Ability to respond promptly to incidents when required.
  • Ability to work nights, weekends, holidays, and varying schedules based on operational needs.
  • Ability to operate radios, mobile reporting applications, access-control systems, CCTV systems, and other security technology.

Core Expectations

The Public Safety Officer serves as a visible, professional, and proactive presence responsible for helping protect people, property, and assets while promoting a safe and welcoming environment.

Public Safety Officers are expected to:

Observe • Deter • Assist • De-escalate • Respond • Report • Protect

The position requires officers to remain actively engaged throughout their shift, maintain strong situational awareness, provide professional assistance to the public, and respond appropriately to security, safety, and emergency situations.

title: 2027 Summer Associate - Atlanta
description:
About The Role

We're a consulting firm built to find growth where others don't see it. Real growth comes from understanding a business inside and out: how it makes money, where its customers are headed, and what has to change to get there. It's spotting the white space competitors miss and turning it into a client's next big move. Our Summer Associate Program is built to teach exactly that, from the ground up.

Over our 8 week internship, Summer Associates work across the firm with colleagues from nearly every discipline in order to solve our client's business challenges. You won't be watching from the sidelines: you'll learn our approach by doing the work itself from research, analysis, and strategy, to the storytelling that ties it together, all pointed at real top-line growth for real clients.

From day one, that means work with real impact for clients and their customers. It means stepping into meaningful responsibility faster than you'd expect, working directly with leaders and clients. It means building next-generation skills that keep you ahead of where business is going. And it means growing a career that connects to what you actually value, not just the client work in front of you.

Your Day to Day

  • Understand the business and the customer
    • You'll dig into industries, markets, and customer behavior to understand how our clients grow, using primary and secondary research to uncover insights that drive transformation.
  • Blend creative and analytical thinking
    • Growth isn’t one lever, it’s brand, culture, digital, marketing, operations, and strategy working together. You'll build the business acumen to know what moves a client's numbers and the creative instinct to bring ideas to life.
  • Synthesize, don't summarize to connect the dots
    • You'll pull together interviews, data, and market scans to form a point of view. You’ll drive value by going beyond AI outputs and reporting desk research findings. You connect the dots others miss and drive to “so what."
  • Contribute to creative problem-solving and storytelling
    • You'll analyze data, shape hypotheses, and turn research into persuasive presentations and frameworks; learning to frame the "so what" and present recommendations to internal leaders and clients.
  • Collaborate on complex challenges across multidisciplinary teams
    • Working alongside multidisciplinary teams, you'll help answer big questions on topics like growth, brand, and transformation from new platforms to market entry; contributing your point of view and refining it through feedback.
  • Explore and work with the full consulting toolkit, incl. AI
    • You'll use the full range of tools in a consultant's toolkit, traditional research and analysis alongside AI, applied where it genuinely helps. We want interns who are able to amplify AI outputs and innovate with new tools and methods.
  • Keep your project moving
    • You'll take ownership of your piece of the work; following through, flagging risks early, and holding yourself accountable for quality and deadlines, not just effort. You'll help keep your project moving; staying close to notes, decisions, and status so nothing gets lost.
  • Play a role beyond project work

ChalkBooks is an AI vertical SaaS startup on a mission to empower millions of students with better educational opportunities and enable tens of thousands of independent schools to become financially sustainable. ChalkBooks is an AI-powered fundraising communication and donor management workflow software purpose-built for schools.

Independent schools heavily rely on fundraising to run themselves, raising billions to give student scholarships and hundreds of billions to construct new buildings and remodel existing ones. At the same time, fundraising offices in independent schools operate much like sales offices in small/medium-sized businesses. Advancement Leaders are metrics-driven and are open to adopting new software to reach their fundraising goals faster.

Building vertical-specific software for fundraising offices in independent schools is a compelling, multi-billion-dollar TAM business opportunity.

Independent schools already pay for old, clunky fundraising software, missing critical school-specific personas and workflows. This legacy fundraising software misses the core job of improving the primary task of school fundraising: building stronger relationships with donors in less time. There is a compelling need for modern, AI-powered fundraising software purpose-built to make communication easier.

What We Are Building

We are building an AI-powered communication, task management, and donor management platform purpose-built for independent schools. Fundraising is one of the oldest professions; however, fundraising in schools is unique due to the number of stakeholders involved and the more complex organizational and human dynamics involved in fundraising in schools (e.g., a current parent of a child can also be a trustee at the school).


Therefore, there is a substantial opportunity to develop several exciting and challenging workflows to speed up and improve how things are done today with the ultimate goal of helping schools raise more.

title: Extrusion Operator
description:
Position Summary

The Foam Extrusion Operator is responsible for setting up, operating, and optimizing foam extrusion lines to produce products that meet dimensional, density, and surface quality specifications. This role requires strong process awareness, attention to detail, and the ability to troubleshoot variations related to gas, temperature, and material blends.



Key Responsibilities

  • Set up foam extrusion lines, including dies, calibrators, cooling systems, pullers, and cutters
  • Start up and shut down extrusion equipment following established procedures
  • Monitor and control critical foam processing parameters such as:
    • Barrel and die temperatures
    • Screw speed and motor load
    • Gas injection and pressure
    • Cooling and vacuum settings
  • Check and maintain product:
    • Density
    • Thickness and dimensions
    • Cell structure and surface finish
  • Make process adjustments to correct issues such as:
    • Density variation
    • Poor cell structure
    • Surface defects
    • Thickness inconsistency
  • Perform product quality checks using scales, calipers, and other measuring tools
  • Record production data, scrap, and process changes accurately
  • Assist with material changes, color changes, and cleanouts
  • Keep hoppers, feed systems, and blending equipment operating correctly
  • Work closely with maintenance and quality teams to resolve line issues
  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area



Required Skills & Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED preferred
  • Manufacturing experience required; foam or plastics extrusion experience strongly preferred
  • Mechanical aptitude and understanding of extrusion equipment
  • Understanding of how temperature, speed, and gas affect foam structure
  • Ability to read measuring devices (tape measure, calipers, scales)
  • Basic math skills (fractions, decimals, conversions)
  • Strong attention to detail and quality
  • Good troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team



Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand for long periods
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs
  • Frequent bending, reaching, and movement around equipment
  • Comfortable working near hot equipment and in a warm production environment



Work Environment

  • Industrial foam extrusion setting
  • Exposure to heat, moving machinery, dust, and production noise
  • Shift work may include nights, weekends, and overtime



Safety Requirements

  • Follow all lockout/tagout procedures
  • Wear required PPE (safety glasses, gloves, hearing protection, etc.)
  • Awareness of hot surfaces, rotating equipment, and pressurized systems (gas injection)
  • Safe handling of raw materials and additives



Preferred (Not Required)

  • Experience with physical or chemical blowing agents
  • Knowledge of density control and cell structure optimization
  • Forklift certification
  • Basic computer and data entry skills

title: Workday Program Manager
description:
EVOCS OVERVIEW

EVOCS was founded with a clear purpose: to help businesses operate more effectively, solve complex challenges, and create opportunities for growth through practical expertise and technology solutions.

As an IT consulting firm, we work with our clients to understand their needs, identify the right technologies, and deliver solutions that improve performance and support their business objectives.

Today, EVOCS is a trusted technology partner to a growing number of organizations and industry leaders. Our team combines technical expertise, business understanding, and a commitment to quality to deliver effective solutions and build lasting client relationships based on responsiveness, consistency, and results.

🎯 Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Workday Program Manager to lead a multi-track Workday implementation currently underway. IT resourcing is solid and a bench of independent subject-matter consultants is already engaged, but the program needs a dedicated business-side leader to own the plan, keep every workstream sequenced, and translate formal program management practice. This is a hands-on, get-it-done role rather than a purely strategic one.

🧩 What you will do

In this role, you will:

Lead the Workday Program Strategy:

  • Own and manage the overall Workday program roadmap, including the work plan, project sequencing, resource planning, and delivery timeline across all active workstreams and future initiatives.
  • Develop and maintain the program work breakdown structure, ensuring cross-functional dependencies are clearly defined and effectively managed.
  • Drive a phased implementation strategy, prioritizing domestic deployments while planning for future international expansion and country-specific requirements.

Drive Cross-Functional Program Execution:

  • Coordinate consultants, internal teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to ensure all workstreams remain aligned and progressing toward program goals.
  • Serve as the hands-on Program Manager, balancing structured program management practices with the organization's current level of operational maturity.
  • Collaborate with the Enterprise Program Management Office (EPMO) to leverage existing governance frameworks, templates, and delivery standards.

Manage Risks and Program Governance:

  • Proactively identify program risks, dependencies, and organizational roadblocks, escalating issues appropriately to executive sponsors and business leadership.
  • Monitor overall program health, timelines, and milestones while providing regular status updates to program sponsors and key stakeholders.
  • Coordinate systems integrator (SI) remobilization and oversee vendor engagement throughout the program lifecycle.

Enable Organizational Success:

  • Translate established project management best practices into practical execution plans that align with the organization's capabilities and evolving needs.
  • Partner with business leaders to navigate organizational complexity, including decentralized teams, evolving job architecture, and Workday capability gaps.
  • Ensure teams remain focused, aligned, and accountable while enabling successful delivery across all program workstreams.

🧠 What you will bring

The top candidate will have the following skills:

  • Proven experience program-managing a Workday implementation (HCM required; Payroll, Financials, or other modules a plus), ideally across multiple concurrent workstreams.
  • Comfort building and maintaining roadmaps, work breakdown structures, and cross-track dependency maps from scratch.
  • Strong vendor and SI management experience, including remobilizing paused engagements.
  • Ability to operate at the maturity level of the organization — pragmatic, adaptable, and focused on progress over process for its own sake.
  • Experience navigating multi-country or multi-entity rollouts, including awareness of international labor requirements, is a plus.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and executive communication skills; comfortable escalating organizational risk without personally trying to resolve it.

Ideally you have…

  • PMP, Workday certification, or equivalent program management credential

title: TPRM Analyst
description:
EVOCS OVERVIEW

EVOCS was founded with a clear purpose: to help businesses operate more effectively, solve complex challenges, and create opportunities for growth through practical expertise and technology solutions.

As an IT consulting firm, we work with our clients to understand their needs, identify the right technologies, and deliver solutions that improve performance and support their business objectives.

TPRM Analyst

EVOCS Overview

EVOCS’s journey began with a mission to empower businesses with advisory expertise, empowered with ideal technologies to provide them with comprehensive solutions to grow and prosper.

Founded by a team of passionate experts, EVOCS has grown into a trusted partner to a growing number of leaders across their respective industries. Our roots in employee-managed operations reflect our commitment to quality, consistency, and client success.

If you enjoy working in a hyper-fast-growing company, are eager to be part of an agile team, and want to be part of our success story, then let’s talk!

🎯 Role Overview

As a TPRM Analyst, you are the execution layer of the third-party risk program. You carry the assessment volume — questionnaires out, evidence in, controls reviewed, findings documented, remediation tracked — and you keep the work moving without needing someone standing behind you.

Two things make or break this role. The first is written documentation: your assessments and findings are read by people who were not on the call, so they have to stand on their own. The second is data quality. A third-party risk program is only worth what its records say, and inconsistent entries quietly erode the value of everything the program produces. If you are the person who notices that two vendors were tiered differently on the same facts, you will do well here.

We are hiring four TPRM Analysts.

🧩 What You Will Do

Assessment Execution

  • Conduct vendor security assessments and third-party reviews across a high-volume queue, on schedule and to a consistent standard
  • Issue and manage security questionnaires, chase evidence requests, and validate what comes back against what was asked for
  • Review control evidence — policies, SOC 2 reports, ISO 27001 certificates, penetration test summaries, and supporting artifacts — and document what the evidence does and does not cover
  • Identify gaps and findings, assign risk ratings under the program’s tiering criteria, and write them up clearly enough that a reader outside the review understands the exposure
  • Escalate complex, contested, or high-criticality reviews to senior analysts with the work already organized

Remediation and Follow-Through

  • Build and track remediation plans with vendors and internal owners, including agreed actions, owners, and due dates
  • Chase stakeholders through to closure — vendors, business owners, procurement, and legal — and keep items from aging out quietly
  • Re-validate evidence at remediation closure rather than accepting a status update at face value
  • Maintain reassessment schedules for in-scope vendors and flag material changes between cycles

Records, Reporting, and Data Quality

  • Own the accuracy and consistency of your entries in the risk register and TPRM platform: complete fields, correct tiering, current status, and traceable evidence links
  • Maintain assessment documentation to an audit-ready standard
  • Produce status reporting on queue volume, aging, findings, and open remediation items
  • Flag inconsistencies in criteria application, data entry, or workflow, and help tighten the process that produced them

🧠 What You Will Bring

title: Project Manager
description:
About the Role

We are looking for a Project Manager (PM) to serve as the project manager for our engineering team. Based in Bengaluru, you’ll be responsible for enabling our product squads to work at maximum speed and effectiveness, ensuring that projects are scoped, tracked, and delivered on time. This is not a back-office role — you’ll be embedded directly with our technical teams, making sure the “machine” of engineering runs smoothly while the engineers focus on building groundbreaking robotics solutions.


You’ll work with modern project management tools like Linear and Github, coordinate across Cologne (DE) and Bengaluru (IN) locations, and keep leadership up-to-date on progress and blockers.


This role is ideal for someone with 3–5 years of project management or program management experience, preferably in software, robotics, or other deep-tech environments, who thrives on clarity, structure, and cross-functional collaboration.

What You'll Do

  • Own project execution: Serve as the project manager for one or more engineering squads, ensuring work is properly scoped, prioritized, and executed.
  • Implement tools and processes: Use project management tools like Linear or Jira to set up workflows, track progress, and provide visibility to leadership.
  • Enable engineers: Free up engineers to focus on solving hard robotics & computer vision problems by ensuring their work is well-structured, dependencies are managed, and blockers are resolved quickly.
  • Coordinate across teams: Act as the bridge between AI/ML engineers, robotics engineers, and leadership to make sure deliverables are aligned and nothing slips through the cracks.
  • Drive accountability: Establish clear ownership of tasks, timelines, and outcomes, and track against them with rigor.
  • Communicate progress: Prepare regular updates for leadership, surfacing risks and highlighting successes.
  • Support global collaboration: Work closely with our offices across locations to ensure seamless coordination between time zones, following eternal.ag's “follow-the-sun” model.
  • Continuously improve: Identify gaps in our engineering workflows and implement process improvements that increase velocity and quality.

Qualifications

Core Requirements (All Levels)

  • 3–5 years of professional experience in project management, program management, or squad operations, ideally in software, robotics, or other engineering-heavy fields.
  • Strong familiarity with Jira, Linear, or equivalent tools, and the ability to design and run project workflows.
  • Proven track record of managing complex projects with multiple stakeholders and deadlines.
  • Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail — you love bringing clarity to complexity.
  • Strong communication skills — able to communicate equally well with engineers and leadership.
  • Proactive problem-solver with a bias for action; you anticipate issues before they become blockers.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced startup environment where priorities can shift quickly.
  • Experience in managing or being part of a PMO.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience in robotics, AI/ML, or deep-tech companies.
  • Agile / Scrum certification or equivalent.
  • Experience coordinating across global teams.
  • Something distinctive that sets you apart — whether that’s leading a major product rollout, implementing innovative workflows, or scaling a project management system from scratch.

Why eternal.ag?

Shape how we scale: This is a chance to design and own the project management backbone of a robotics company. You’ll set up processes, tools, and ways of working that will define how eternal.ag’s engineering teams deliver at scale.

Build from scratch: Rather than inheriting a legacy system, you’ll implement and refine workflows that enable a fast-moving, global engineering team to operate with clarity and focus.

Impact at Scale: Your work will directly contribute to solving global food security challenges. We're building technology to transform 800,000 hectares of greenhouses worldwide into sustainable, autonomous food production facilities.

Growth Opportunity: Join as we scale from proof-of-concept to global deployment and shape the DNA of how the company executes for years to come. Be part of the core team shaping the future of horticultural automation.

Flexible Work Culture: Distributed team with offices in Cologne and Bengaluru, following a "follow-the-sun" support model for our 24/7 operations.

Apply Now

Ready to revolutionize how the world grows food? Join us in building autonomous systems that will feed billions while conserving resources and eliminating the dependency on seasonal labor.


We're committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experience levels who are excited about our mission and show potential to grow with us. Recent graduates - don't let experience requirements hold you back; we value passion, potential, and fresh perspectives.



eternal.ag is building fully automated food production sites that can sustainably produce fresh food year-round. Backed by world-class investors and partnering with leading agricultural companies, we're turning the vision of fully-autonomous greenhouses into reality.

Location - Canberra | On-site, with occasional remote flexibility subject to project requirements

Our purpose is to deliver mission critical technology solutions tailored for the Australian defence, government and national security sectors. We specialise in high security data systems, designed to meet Australia's evolving strategic and operational demands. If you are ready to turn your expertise into real world results, welcome to Bluestaq Australia. This is your opportunity to join a young but fast growing company in its formative years in Australia, building on our successful foundations in the United States.

About the Role
As Cybersecurity Engineer, you will lead the design, implementation and oversight of cybersecurity architecture for defence grade systems across networks, platforms and on-premise environments. You will work across engineering and operations teams to ensure the integrity, compliance and resilience of secure systems in accordance with Australian standards and mission critical needs.

You will be instrumental in securing and maintaining an Authority to Operate (ATO) by implementing technical controls, conducting risk assessments and ensuring compliance with the Australian ISM, IRAP (Infosec Registered Assessors Program) and other defence frameworks.

Reporting to the Bluestaq Australia leadership team, you will:

  • Define and enforce cybersecurity standards in alignment with NIST, ISO/IEC 27001 and the ASD Essential Eight
  • Support the preparation and submission of cybersecurity artifacts required for ATO processes, including security documentation, risk registers and evidence packages
  • Implement and validate technical security controls in classified environments aligned with Australian ISM and ACSC requirements
  • Develop and deploy security tools to address vulnerabilities, automate tasks and strengthen defences
  • Conduct comprehensive risk assessments, vulnerability testing and security audits
  • Hands-on configuration and monitoring of security tools, analysing logs and security events to detect, assess and respond to threats
  • Collaborate with engineering teams to implement secure authentication, encryption and access control solutions
  • Evaluate and integrate emerging cybersecurity technologies to enhance infrastructure protection
  • Clearly articulate security strategies and collaborate with cross-functional teams to support secure solution delivery
  • Provide expert level troubleshooting and resolution of complex security challenges

About You

You must be willing to embrace our core values of Ownership, Curiosity, Talent and Trust and in addition have:

  • 6–8+ years of cybersecurity experience, preferably in defence, government or critical infrastructure sectors
  • Relevant tertiary qualification or equivalent knowledge gained through experience
  • CISSP certification (or equivalent), plus ASD recognised cybersecurity credentials
  • Strong expertise in Linux systems, networking security and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP)
  • Hands-on experience with security automation and monitoring tools, including Ansible, SIEM platforms (e.g., Splunk, SO2), antivirus (AV) solutions, ACAS, Anchore, SonarQube, and related security technologies
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cybersecurity initiatives, influence architecture decisions and communicate effectively with stakeholders
  • Willingness to travel within Australia to customer and partner locations, including secure government or defence sites, and occasional travel to Bluestaq offices in the United States for collaboration or project work.

Together, we’ll tackle high stakes challenges, protect Australia's most vital data and build what’s next, securely, on-premises and at scale.

title: Budget Analyst
description:
SCT is a firm that partners and collaborates with our clients to deliver results and navigate complex challenges. We bring specialized expertise in strategic planning, organizational effectiveness, data analytics, talent management, human capital management, and PMO services. Our core values, that we apply to everything we do, are Integrity, Superior Value, Excellence, Teamwork, Empowerment and Continuous Learning.

We value highly and therefore cultivate a collaborative working culture that emphasizes each employee's strengths and interests in building our team and delivering for clients.

This requisition is for proposal staffing purposes. Employment is contingent upon contract award.

Position Summary

SCT is seeking a Budget Analyst to support financial planning, budget formulation, execution, and reporting activities. This role will work closely with program leadership, finance teams, and client stakeholders to ensure accurate budget tracking, compliance with federal regulations, and data driven financial decision making.

Duties

  • Develop, analyze, and manage budgets in support of program and organizational objectives
  • Prepare budget forecasts, financial reports, and cost projections
  • Support budget formulation processes, including data collection, analysis, and submission preparation
  • Conduct financial analysis to support strategic planning and resource allocation decisions
  • Ensure compliance with applicable federal regulations, contract requirements, and internal policies
  • Collaborate with program managers and stakeholders to provide budget guidance and recommendations
  • Analyze historical data and trends to improve budget accuracy and forecasting
  • Support audits, reviews, and financial reporting requirements
  • Utilize financial systems and tools to track and report on budget performance

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Mathematics, Social Science, or a related field
  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience in budget analysis, financial management, or a closely related field
  • Active U.S. Government security clearance with fully adjudicated T5 background investigation including drug test
  • Familiarity with federal budget processes and experience in government consulting is preferred
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and quantitative skills
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial reporting tools
  • Experience preparing and presenting financial data to stakeholders
  • Strong work ethic with excellent organizational and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to interact professionally with clients
  • Exceptional written and oral communication skills

Location
DC Metro Area; onsite

Supervisory role
No

Salary
$100,000 to $140,000, commensurate with education and experience

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

title: DevOps Engineer (Mission-Critical Systems)
description:
About the role

As a DevOps Engineer, you will collaborate closely with operations teams to understand existing processes, identify bottlenecks, and develop solutions that modernize legacy architectures. You will help automate business processes and support modernization efforts, such as cloud migrations and application containerization.

What you'll do

  • Collaborate with operations teams to understand current processes and pain points, and propose modernization strategies.
  • Develop solutions that automate manual business processes and streamline operations.
  • Work with complex satellite-based data at all stages including ingest, processing, and dissemination.
  • Support efforts to modernize legacy systems, including cloud migrations, containerizations, and infrastructure updates.
  • Design and implement cloud-based solutions in AWS environments.
  • Leverage DevOps practices such as infrastructure as code (IaC), CI/CD pipelines, and configuration management to ensure efficient deployment and scalability.
  • Design, implement, and optimize monitoring systems using the TIG stack (Telegraf, InfluxDB, Grafana).
  • Work in agile environments, participating in sprints and iterative development to deliver high-quality software products.
  • Deploy applications in containerized environments (e.g., Docker) and ensure smooth integration in mixed Linux and Windows environments.

Qualifications

  • Expertise in cloud software and AWS services (e.g., EC2, S3, Lambda, RDS, CloudFormation).
  • Hands-on experience developing solutions in AWS cloud environments.
  • Previous experience modernizing legacy architectures and applications and implementing automated solutions.
  • Strong knowledge of infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform, Ansible) and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience deploying and optimizing the TIG stack (Telegraf, InfluxDB, Grafana).
  • Expertise with containerization tools (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) and cloud-native solutions.
  • Familiarity with both Windows and Linux operating environments.
  • Experience with Bash shell scripting, Perl, Python, and/or C#.
  • Experience with Jira projects and Confluence for documentation and collaboration.
  • Experience supporting federal government mission environments, especially NOAA/NESDIS, is highly preferred.
Education and Experience
  • BS in Computer Science, Engineering, related disciplines or equivalent.
  • 6+ years of experience in software development/engineering.
Must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident who has lived in the United States for at least 3 of the last 5 years and be able to pass a background investigation to obtain a security badge to access applicable government facilities and systems.

title: Civil Project Designer | Ann Arbor, MI
description:
Civil Project Designer | Ann Arbor, MI

100% Employee-Owned · Big-firm resources, local-team relationships, ONE IMEG culture

IMEG is hiring a Civil Project Designer in Ann Arbor, MI, to lead civil design efforts on low to moderate complexity projects and collaborate with senior staff on larger, high complexity work. This role works closely with engineers and consultants to deliver engineering solutions, field inspections, reports, permit applications, and site drainage and grading designs that support positive client outcomes.

You will contribute to project planning, budgeting, scheduling, mentoring, and cross-functional coordination while supporting industrial and manufacturing work. The team also brings experience in technical industrial environments and production-support infrastructure, with recurring work tied to automotive R&D, chemical process, and manufacturing support, while delivering resilient, environmentally responsible infrastructure.

At a Glance

Location: Ann Arbor, MI

Discipline: Civil

Markets: Industrial; Manufacturing; MEP

Ownership: 100% employee-owned (ESOP)

Travel: Up to 10%

Work Schedule: Full-time hybrid

Sponsorship: Not available

What You'll Do

  • Direct and train Civil Design Technicians to support reports, exhibits, plans, specifications, and permit applications required by the project’s contractual scope.
  • Lead design efforts for low to moderate complexity civil site design projects across commercial, residential, and industrial work.
  • Utilize engineering software and tools to create detailed designs, specifications, and calculations according to code requirements and IMEG standards.
  • Complete and oversee permit applications in coordination with the team, client, and reviewing jurisdiction.
  • Oversee projects through bidding and construction administration.
  • Work with clients to understand needs, gather project requirements, communicate technical information effectively, and build professional relationships.
  • Support consulting-project execution as part of a project team.
  • Lead project planning, budgeting, and scheduling tasks; document client design decisions and instructions; and monitor design progress, percent complete, and fee expended.
  • Analyze engineering problems, propose innovative solutions, and collaborate with senior engineers and consultants to develop practical and efficient solutions.
  • Prioritize safety and regulatory compliance, interpret state and local design criteria, and apply them to specific project needs.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, including other engineers, architects, and project managers, to deliver integrated solutions.
  • Identify potential project problems and seek advice from the Project Manager.

What You'll Bring

Required

Education

  • Bachelor of Science (BS) Degree in Civil Engineering, or equivalent required

Experience

  • 3 years of experience minimum required, 4 preferred, in the building design consulting industry OR
  • 7 years of experience minimum required, 8 preferred, in the building design consulting or construction industry

Required Skills/Abilities

  • Knowledge of industry standard engineering software, primarily Civil 3D
  • Proficient with pipe networking and road corridors.
  • Proficiency in design techniques, tools, and concepts involved in the production of technical plans and specifications
  • Strong technical and analytical skills including proficiency of principles in the civil engineering field
  • Ability to train and mentor less experienced staff
  • Able to lead teams with others that utilize industry standard software that assists with civil engineering analysis and design
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; Ability to clearly communicate in both oral and written communication to individuals or groups
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment
  • Attention to detail and problem-solving skills
  • Eagerness to adapt to new challenges
  • Proficient with MS Office Suite including but not limited to Word, Excel, and Outlook
  • Ability to travel up to 10% with occasional overnight stays

Preferred

  • Engineer-In-Training (EIT) certification preferred
  • Associates degree, or certificate, in utilizing Autodesk Civil 3D or equivalent software tools or engineering preferred

About the Team

  • The team is process- and manufacturing-oriented, with strong mechanical, electrical, process engineering, and automation/controls involvement.
  • Its portfolio includes recurring automotive R&D, chemical process, manufacturing support, and some civil and municipal utility work.
  • The team is especially strong in technical industrial environments and production-support infrastructure.
  • Recent work includes Rockford International Airport / Terminal Remoel / Phase 2 - Departures, Transportation; 3M/Misc 2017, Industrial; and Bee Branch / Stormwater Pumping Station, Government (City/County/State).

Why IMEG

We put people at the center of who we are, creating positive outcomes for people, communities, and our planet.

  • Employee ownership (ESOP), fully vested at all times, with a 3% to 6% company contribution, plus year-end profit sharing
  • IDEA Program: a firm-wide innovation accelerator where employees across every discipline develop and scale new tools, from VR and AI to carbon-reduction technology
  • PE, SE, and other license exam prep and support, with a clear path from EIT to PE
  • Dress for Your Day flexibility (wear what fits your day)
  • Generous time off, including 6 paid holidays and 3 additional floating holidays
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage starting day one, with preventive care at 100%, a $50/month wellness credit, and a Calm subscription
  • MEG, our in-house AI platform, helps employees find information and build agents that streamline project workflows and calculations

Bring Your Career to IMEG

Apply today and join a team delivering thoughtful civil engineering solutions that support clients, projects, and communities.

title: Engineer I, Digital Engagement
description:
About You

You’re early in your engineering career and hungry to to use your engineering skills to have an immediate impact on the world.You might not have seen every design pattern or system failure yet, but you learn fast, ask good questions, and aren’t afraid to dive into a codebase to figure out how it really works.

You’re curious, adaptable, and energized by the idea that code can drive real-world outcomes. You don’t just want to polish small bugs in the background. You want ownership, responsibility, and the opportunity to level up quickly by working alongside experienced engineers and shipping work that has visible impact.

At Tavern, skills matter more than credentials. We don’t care if you took a non-traditional path or left school early. Our engineers use AI coding agents almost exclusively — we’re constantly testing new models and new workflows, and coding by hand is a distant memory around here. If that excites you, you’ll fit right in.

Political experience is a plus, not a requirement. If our mission resonates with you, we encourage you to apply, even if you don’t check every box.

About the Role

As an Engineer I at Tavern, you’ll be a core builder on the team, turning real requirements into working software, and understanding why we’re building what we’re building.

This is a hands-on, execution-focused role. You’ll write production code, write tests, and help get features across the finish line. You’ll work closely with senior engineers who will review your work, challenge your thinking, and help support your technical growth.

Your work might include instrumenting an experiment to measure impact, building out our sentiment-measurement tooling, or improving how we cross-validate results with survey data.

We value in-person collaboration and expect regular time in our Chicago office. We’re hiring multiple engineers and reviewing applications on a rolling basis—if the posting is still up, the position is still open.

About the Team: Digital Engagement

You’d be joining the team that builds tools to understand conversation on major social platforms. We build systems for large-scale sentiment measurement and experimentation, and we partner closely with our Surveys team to validate what’s working.

This team supports fast-moving, time-sensitive campaigns, so you’ll get hands-on experience with experiment design, measurement infrastructure, and rapid iteration — with visibility into the real-world impact of your work.

Responsibilities

  • Translate product and internal requirements into clean, functioning code that ships to production.
  • Work closely with the engineering team to implement solutions, write unit tests, and participate in code reviews.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues in production, contributing to the stability and reliability of our tools.
  • Use LLMs and AI coding tools to accelerate development and continuously expand your technical skill set.
  • Actively participate in planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives to improve how we build and ship software.

Qualifications

  • 0-2+ years of relevant experience, with an emphasis on demonstrated ability rather than tenure.
  • Proficiency in Python, JavaScript and Docker.
  • Experience working with and deploying LLMs or agentic, AI-assisted systems.
  • Experience building backend systems, including working with databases, APIs, and infrastructure, with a solid understanding of core data structures and algorithms.
  • Experience with (or strong interest in) social platform APIs, data pipelines, or experiment/measurement systems is a plus.
  • Familiarity with modern development tools such as Docker, Git/version control, and basic CI/CD workflows.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously in a fast moving environment.

To be explicit, you don’t need a degree to work here. You just need to be good at the things we’re asking from you.

title: Clinical Supervisor (LCSW/LMFT)
description:
In a world of noise, we find the signal — the pulse of potential. We weave the strands of talent, vision, and purpose into organizations that endure. Blending intelligence with intuition, we honor the human art of connection at the heart of every great company.

About the Job

This search is a little different for us.

At Signal & Strand, we believe the best work we do is not always measured by revenue. While much of our work focuses on helping organizations build exceptional teams and leadership capabilities, we occasionally take on select searches on a pro bono basis for organizations whose missions we deeply believe in.

This is one of those searches.

We are partnered with a leading nonprofit organization serving women experiencing homelessness on the search for a Clinical Supervisor (LCSW/LMFT).

Reporting to the Clinical Director, this individual will provide clinical leadership, supervision, and oversight across behavioral health programs, including a Trauma Recovery Center serving women navigating complex challenges related to trauma, mental health, substance use, and housing instability.

This is an opportunity for a licensed clinician who is passionate about developing other clinicians, strengthening trauma-informed service delivery, and ensuring high-quality care for one of Los Angeles' most vulnerable populations.

The Clinical Supervisor will oversee a team of four clinicians, with an additional opening planned, and will assume responsibility for both individual and group supervision immediately upon joining the organization.

The Mandate

This organization is seeking a leader who can balance empathy with accountability.

The team is comprised of dedicated clinicians doing important work in a complex environment. What is needed now is a supervisor who can support, coach, and develop staff while also establishing clear expectations around documentation, performance, and clinical excellence.

Documentation quality and timeliness are critical priorities for this team. The ideal candidate will be comfortable holding the line on standards, addressing gaps directly, and creating systems that help clinicians stay on track without sacrificing quality of care.

This is not a role with a direct client caseload. Instead, the focus is on supervision, leadership, staff development, program oversight, and ensuring clinicians have the support and structure they need to be successful.

Success in this role will require strong clinical judgment, experience managing performance and accountability, and the ability to develop clinicians into stronger practitioners and future leaders.

The organization places a significant emphasis on promoting from within and investing in leadership development, creating meaningful opportunities for long-term growth and advancement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide individual and group clinical supervision to unlicensed clinicians working toward licensure
  • Deliver ongoing clinical consultation, coaching, and support to clinicians across programs
  • Review and approve clinical documentation in accordance with organizational and regulatory standards
  • Support day-to-day operations of the Trauma Recovery Center and ensure grant compliance requirements are met
  • Monitor documentation quality, timeliness, and overall clinical performance
  • Provide guidance during crises and model effective de-escalation and intervention techniques
  • Train, develop, and support a multidisciplinary team delivering trauma-informed services
  • Lead onboarding, training, and professional development initiatives for clinical staff
  • Analyze program data, identify trends and service gaps, and support quality improvement efforts
  • Prepare reports and leverage data to inform operational and clinical decision-making
  • Utilize systems including Excel and electronic health record platforms to monitor program performance and documentation compliance
  • Attend funder meetings and support ongoing program compliance
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with community partners, service providers, and stakeholders
  • Facilitate clinical meetings, group supervision sessions, and staff trainings
  • Serve as an ambassador for the organization within the community

Ideal Profile

  • Active California LCSW or LMFT license in good standing
  • Minimum two years of post-licensure experience
  • Completion of a 15-hour Clinical Supervision training program
  • Prior supervisory experience required
  • Demonstrated experience holding staff accountable while maintaining a supportive and collaborative culture
  • Strong crisis intervention experience
  • Experience working with individuals experiencing homelessness, trauma, mental illness, and substance use disorders
  • Familiarity with evidence-based practices including Trauma-Informed Care, CBT, DBT, Harm Reduction, Motivational Interviewing, and Seeking Safety
  • Strong report writing, documentation review, and data analysis capabilities
  • Experience identifying operational gaps and implementing process improvements
  • Proficiency with Excel and electronic health record systems; experience with Exym is a plus
  • Strong leadership, coaching, and team development capabilities
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining high standards of care and documentation
  • Cultural humility and experience serving diverse populations, including communities disproportionately impacted by homelessness
  • Spanish language proficiency is a plus

Location & Work Model

Los Angeles, California

Hybrid schedule with three days per week onsite and two days remote.

Candidates must reside in California and live within 80 miles of the organization's office.

title: Risk Officer NOC
description:
DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS

27 September 2026-23:59-GMT+02:00 Eastern European Standard Time (Cairo)

WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability.


ABOUT WFP

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of climate change.


At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok.

WHY JOIN WFP?

  • WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.

  • WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.

  • WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.

  • A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.

  • We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement).

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:

This position is located in Cairo with the Global HQ MENAEERO, job holder is part of the Risk Management Division, reports to the Regional Risk Officer and supports risk management activities in the regional offices and in Country Offices.

JOB PURPOSE:

Provide advice and specialized support in the establishment of risk assessment and risk management activities, application of controls and compliance with policies and procedures; and contribute to the overall

effectiveness of operations and optimization of WFP resources.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:

  • Contribute to embedding risk management in planning and decision-making through the regular updating of risk registers, development and monitoring of key risk appetite metrics and risk indicators, including progress towards implementing the risk mitigation actions.

  • Participate and/or facilitate during regular and ad hoc risk assessments in regional, country and field offices with relevant managers to: identify policy and procedure gaps resulting from emerging operational condition; identify and assess risks; contribute to the development and design of mitigation actions; assess effectiveness of internal controls.

  • Contribute to the discussion with functional experts, including in Risk Committees and other committees, on: identifying trends and emerging issues; preparation of guidance material and checklists in conformity with WFP policies and rules on periodic risk and/or control assessments; linking risk, oversight and evaluation information. Serve as liaison with GHQ oversight including OIG, Ethics, Legal and Evaluations ensuring operational efficiency and compliance.

  • Review and analyse risk management activities, exposures and mitigation actions in draft Country Strategic Plan (CSP)/Interim CSP including budget revisions.

  • Support timely risk and/or incident escalation, assist and advise CO management to ensure compliance with corporate escalation protocols. Handle fraud related complaints received through community feedback mechanisms and assess the materiality of fraud incidents, when delegated. Serve as CO management liaison with Officer of Inspector & Investigations for reporting, monitoring and control remediation measures.

  • Maintain incident reporting and case tracking by ensuring timely follow-up and documentation, including monitoring trends and escalation timelines.

  • Support engagement with donors and consolidate inputs related to donor risk-sharing arrangements, including risk assessments and mitigation strategies. Deliver strategic risk-related documentation and analysis to support senior management decision-making, donor engagement, and resource mobilization efforts.

  • Conduct the annual Executive Director’s Assurance exercise (e.g., collect and review and clear inputs for the survey). Provide expert advice to CO management on complex risk and accountability issues, promote enhancement and/or establish adequate internal control systems with clear accountabilities and maintain an effective internal control environment to support operational efficiency.

  • Promote accountability across functional units, manage the review/preparation of comprehensive periodic progress reports summarising the status of compliance of internal controls, key oversight themes, and using risk information (e.g., risk indicators, incidents) to highlight areas out of risk appetite and formulate sound recommendations on required actions in areas of vulnerability.

  • Support managers to prepare, plan for and implement Internal Audit and External Audit exercises (e.g., collect and analyse essential documents, coordinate briefing meetings and follow-up on recommendations including maintaining a repository).

  • Using the Three Lines Model, contribute to the development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) by First Line colleagues for managing the risk and compliance process, including criteria for conducting and following up on risk management oversight missions, training materials and modules, etc., to minimize risk to the organization. As part of second-line, strengthen oversight role by conducting and/or coordinating management oversight missions

  • Promote and disseminate the revised anti-fraud and anti-corruption (AFAC) policy and WFP’s adherence to Zero Tolerance for Inaction, including supporting managers in their fact-finding reviews and fraud risk assessments. Support collection and analysis of data on fraud incidents, fraud risk metrics, and fraud risk appetite, providing training in AFAC standards.

  • Coordinate Business Continuity Management activities by developing and maintaining the BCM Plan and booklets, as well as and responding to the activation of business continuity procedures.

  • Assess information/training needs and prepare and deliver training programmes or information sessions for colleagues and partners in RO or CO to enhance understanding of risk management and compliance with WFP policies, rules, regulations and procedures.

  • Other duties as required, including potentially serving as Organizational Conflicts of Interest (OCI) focal point (e.g., supporting OCI avoidance plans and procedures).

DESIRED EXPERIENCES FOR ENTRY INTO THE ROLE:

  • Hands-on knowledge of governance, organizational structures, strategy and major initiatives of international organizations.

  • Demonstrable experience in programme/project management

title: Cluster Leader
description:
Why we need you

Springboard Collaborative closes the literacy gap by closing the gap between home and school. We coach educators and family members to help kids learn to read by 4th grade. Springboard envisions a world in which all children have the requisite literacy skills to access life opportunities.


The Cluster Leader will be responsible for leading Springboard programming across all school sites in their cluster. As part of their work, the Cluster Leader will supervise the Program Leaders and teachers in their cluster and will report to the Program Director. This is a great opportunity to support families and to help students accelerate their progress in learning to read.


This is a fixed-term, non-benefits-eligible, part-time position with up to 110 total work hours over 15 weeks. The Springboard Cluster Leader must commit to on-the-ground support at Philadelphia schools during after-school hours. It requires 10 hours of pre-programming professional development. Employment terms coincide with student registration and the program dates set forth by the District.



You can read more about the goals, responsibilities, competencies, and requirements below. We'd love to have you join us!

This is important

We are an equal opportunity employer. Diversity is more than a commitment at Springboard Collaborative—it’s at the core of what we do and how we do it. No one can solve a problem better than those who experience it firsthand. That’s why Springboard aspires to hire a diverse team that reflects the marginalized communities we serve.


We also know that having a diverse workforce makes for a better workplace. Springboard’s hiring process seeks individuals who value diversity across race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, national origin, and more.


Finally, if you’re passionate about an open role, we encourage you to apply— even if you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications listed on the job description!

Here are your goals as a Cluster Leader:

  • 100% registration to target enrollment
  • 90% family workshop attendance
  • 88% daily student attendance
  • 80% students achieve their growth goals

Here are your responsibilities within and beyond the first year:

Support programming

  • Serve as liaison between Springboard Collaborative, building administration, Springboard staff, enrichment staff, and participating students and families
  • Ensure adherence to daily programming schedule
  • Monitor crucial programmatic data, setting high expectations for teachers to do the same
  • Cultivate a positive and achievement-driven culture centered around student reading growth, family collaboration, and program fidelity

Coach and manage teachers

  • Support Program Leaders in achieving their personal-professional goals
  • Lead weekly program implementation/coaching meetings with direct reports
  • Support weekly Professional Learning Community (PLC) meetings to prepare leaders and teachers for family workshops, high-quality instruction and data analysis
  • Observe instruction and Family Workshops–provide regular feedback to leaders and teachers
  • Participate in regular city leadership meetings with Program Director
  • Co-facilitate bi-weekly CityWide meetings

Build partnerships with family members

  • Support enrollment and team huddles to achieve 100% completion
  • Support outreach for family workshops and other family engagement events and support make-up workshops as necessary

Utilize data to meet performance metrics

  • Review key data points, such as student attendance, family workshop attendance, assessment data, family survey data, and other relevant metrics
  • Participate in weekly meetings with a Springboard Program Director, utilizing data to inform and drive effective next steps

Additional responsibilities

  • Maintain regular communication with school leaders, assisting in planning and scheduling meetings with administrators
  • Respond to unforeseen needs and challenges

What you offer us

Here are the competencies and requirements we expect the right candidate to have:

  • You are a literacy expert with extensive knowledge of PreK-3rd grade content.
  • You are a problem solver who effectively utilizes data to achieve program goals.
  • You are a coach who can support reports as they work toward professional goals.
  • You have experience leveraging data management systems and visualization tools to track student progress.
  • You bring a high level of tech fluency, particularly in utilizing technology for collecting, analyzing, and interpreting program and student data.
  • You are a skilled relationship builder, fostering meaningful collaboration with families.
  • You possess exceptional communication, organization, and critical thinking skills.
  • You are a firm believer in our collective opportunity to close the literacy gap through hard work and collaboration with families.

Nice to have:

  • You have experience with the Philadelphia School District.

While this description is meant to provide an overview of the responsibilities and requirements of the Cluster Leader, we are seeking candidates who demonstrate flexibility and can adapt to evolving needs in an entrepreneurial environment.

What we offer you

Compensation

This role will receive hourly compensation of $55/hour.

Location and travel

This role will be a hybrid role involving both virtual coaching and in-person on-site work at the Philadelphia schools in your assigned cluster.


Springboard requires in-person employees at a Springboard facility or participating in in-person programming or events to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 unless a medical or religious exemption is approved. Being fully vaccinated means an individual is at least two weeks past their final dose of a CDC-authorized COVID-19 vaccine regimen. As a condition of employment, newly hired employees may be asked to provide their COVID-19 vaccination status and proof of vaccination, as required.


Please note that this employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

About Springboard Collaborative

Since our founding in 2012, we have grown Springboard’s reach from 40 to more than 100,000 students in over 300 Title 1 schools. Amidst rapid growth, Springboard consistently delivers best-in-class results. In schools that often struggle to get 20% of parents to show up for report card conferences, Springboard’s weekly family workshops average 88% attendance. Students average a 3-4-month reading gain during each program cycle, closing the gap to grade-level performance by about half in just five or ten weeks. Springboard’s work has been featured by Forbes, NPR, and the New York Times (twice). Nationally, Springboard Collaborative is the only organization to have cracked the code on equipping marginalized families to teach reading at home. You can learn more by watching our CEO on the main stage of ASU GSV. You can also read more about how we engage teachers and families to accelerate student learning in this op-ed.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
Citrus Health Group is a new type of agency that brings an empathetic patient focus to the new product commercialization process. Citrus creates hand-picked teams that provide clients with scientific, clinical, pharmacologic, evidence-generation, pricing and reimbursement, market access, affordability, and patient support expertise and experience in their time of need. Client teams are built with talented experts who function as a fluid, agile, and highly energized team.

We are passionate about science; our focus is to effectively communicate science in compelling and engaging ways to drive true value and enable patients to gain access to new medicines. We do so with the highest level of integrity and respect for the ethical nature of our business.

We invite you to join our talented team of dedicated professionals, working closely together to provide the services our clients need, at the time they need them. We are driven by one word, RESPECT. We respect each other, we respect our clients, and we respect the professionals we work with on behalf of our clients. We value every team member and strive for an inclusive and collaborative culture that fosters the best in everyone.

About the Opportunity

Under the direction of the Project Management Lead, the Senior Project Manager will partner with internal stakeholders (Account, Scientific & Medical Services, Editorial, Creative and Finance teams) in the development and execution of client deliverables. Demonstrating project ownership, the Senior Project Manager will possess and convey a comprehensive knowledge of the status and timelines for all tactics assigned to the respective internal client team. To ensure the seamless delivery of publications, multichannel medical communications tactics and activities, the Senior Project Manager will develop and implement timelines; communicate effectively and thoughtfully with colleagues, clients, and all external stakeholders; think strategically and take a proactive approach to problem-solving; and monitor project budgets in close consultation with Client Services and Central Services to track and manage invoicing of all projects.

We are seeking candidates for both freelance and full time opportunities.

Responsibilities

Client Service, Project Planning, Management, and Tracking

  • Assume overall project-level ownership and responsibility for publication accounts, including determining and refining specifications ahead of project initiation and tracking and maintaining the status of projects and their respective scopes, timelines, budgets, and deliverables
    • Proactively manage the account and be responsive to the client’s expectations and needs in project execution on a timely basis
  • Draft workflows/timelines (using resources available) and review to ensure they are drafted accurately
  • Formally initiate projects within WorkBook and with internal team members, alerting team members when project scope/budget has been approved and work may begin
  • Own the integrity and accuracy of the status report and other client deliverables while maximizing the role of other colleagues in the preparation of these documents
  • Draft recap of key takeaways for team ﬁnalization
  • Ensure that client meeting materials (e.g., agenda, slides, meeting minutes, etc.) are accurately prepared
  • Assume ownership and responsibility for author relationships and their assigned tasks; remits include distribution and tracking of/follow-up on author responses to (or completion of) invitations, agreements, forms, and drafted or final deliverables; maintaining an archive of all these communications on the Citrus Health Group server (SharePoint)
  • Own entries within client project tracking software (e.g., iEnvision, DataVision, PubsHub, PubStrat); remits may include creation and management of project entries, creation of review workflows, maintenance of any project checklists in the system, and final project audit and closure once completed
  • Submits information to client databases (Veeva Vault, Zinc) for tracking physician payments, travel, meals, and gifts (Sunshine Act)

Financial Management and Tracking: Overall responsibility for the integrity and accuracy of financial deliverables (i.e., budgets, invoices, trackers, etc.)

  • Work with the account team to draft, submit, monitor, and adhere to approved budgets
  • Maintain accurate ﬁnancial spreadsheet(s) to support internal and client needs

Assume overall project-level ownership and responsibility for WorkBook entries, including creation, updates, monitoring, and closure of budgets; all project invoices; and tracking project expenses and vendor POs

  • Draft scope and budget (using Word and WorkBook templates) for any fixed-fee projects, as applicable per client
  • Work with teams to submit invoices and accruals in a timely manner consistent with both internal and client-directed SOPs
  • Prepare for and be accountable for actions discussed in monthly revenue meetings
  • Create vendor POs within WorkBook; initiate/track internal review and approval of PO ahead of PO being provided to vendor
  • Prepare work-in-progress and revenue reconciliation monitoring/report updates on a bimonthly or monthly basis and in financial tracking and forecasting across accounts

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree
  • 4-5 years of experience in project management within a medical communications agency, publications, and/or pharmaceutical company
  • Experience with publication accounts within a medical communications agency and with iEnvision software is required
  • High level of integrity, confidence, and accountability
  • Effective organizational skills; attention to detail and timelines; high degree of accuracy
  • Excellent ﬁnancial acumen
  • Ability to coordinate and execute multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to evaluate, interpret, and analyze both written and verbal communications
  • Ability to coach junior team members in a way that is conducive to their growth
  • Understanding of industry guidelines, regulations, and requirements
  • Well-developed professional communication skills, including written and interpersonal
  • Strong sense of diplomacy, including solid negotiation, conflict resolution, and people management skills
  • Ability to master various content management systems
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel)
  • Travel as required
